* Vocabulary:
(سَبِيلِي): al-sabīl is the road, or the clear part of it; it is treated as masculine and feminine, and the plural is subul, subl, asbul, asbila and subūl. Ibn al-sabīl is the traveller. Sabīl Allāh is jihad, seeking knowledge, the pilgrimage and every good thing Allah has commanded. One says: «laysa laka ʿalayya sabīl», that is, you have no argument against me to hold to; and «laysa ʿalayya fī kadhā sabīl», that is, there is no blame on me in such-and-such. The post-classical speakers (al-muwalladūn) say: «mā ʿalā al-muḥsin sabīl», that is, there is no opposing the one who does good; and «sabīlunā an nafʿala kadhā», that is, we are worthy of doing it.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ هذِهِ سَبِيلِي أَدْعُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ عَلى بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِي): (هذه) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (سبيلي) the khabar (predicate). The clause «أدعو الله» [Translator's note: so in the source, for (أدعو إلى الله)] is an explanation of «the way». (إلى الله) is attached to (أدعو). The clause may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ, but the first is preferable. (على بصيرة) is attached to (أدعو), or to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of (أدعو). (أنا) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) agent of (أدعو), and (من اتبعني) is conjoined to the latent agent of (أدعو). (من) may also be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is: "and whoever follows me also calls". (أنا) may also be a postponed mubtadaʾ, with (على بصيرة) a fronted khabar and (من اتبعني) conjoined to (أنا).
(وَسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ وَما أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): (وسبحان) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, that is: "and I glorify, glorifying Allah". (وما): the wāw is a conjunction and (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative; (أنا) is its noun and (من المشركين) its predicate.
(وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجالًا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقُرى): (ما) is negative; (أرسلنا) is a verb and its agent; (من قبلك) is a ḥāl; (إلا) is the particle of restriction; (رجالا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (نوحي إليهم) is a naʿt (adjective), and (من أهل القرى) is a second adjective of (رجالا).
(أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ): the hamza is for interrogation and the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, as explained earlier. (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive; (يسيروا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يسيروا).
(فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): the fāʾ is conjunctive or causative. (ينظروا) is an imperfect verb, either jussive by being coordinated with (يسيروا), or accusative by an implied an in reply to the negation. (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted predicate of (كان); (عاقبة) is the noun of (كان); (الذين) is the muḍāf ilayhi of (عاقبة); and (من قبلهم) is attached to an omitted [verb], the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
(وَلَدارُ الْآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial and the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ). (دار) is the mubtadaʾ and (الآخرة) is the muḍāf ilayhi, a case of annexing a thing to itself, since what is meant by "the abode" is Paradise, which is itself the Hereafter. Al-Zamakhsharī and al-Bayḍāwī preferred the implied form "and the abode of the last Hour" or "of the last state", so on that view there is no annexing of a thing to itself in the speech.
(خير) is the predicate of (دار); (للذين) is attached to (خير); and the clause (اتقوا) is the ṣila. (أفلا تعقلون): its i'rab has preceded.
(حَتَّى إِذَا اسْتَيْأَسَ الرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُوا): (حتى) is a particle of limit, attached to something omitted indicated by the speech, as if it were said: "We sent before you only men, and their victory was delayed until, when they despaired of victory…". It is not necessary that Allah had promised them victory in this world; rather they thought so and hoped for it, not on the basis of any report or revelation. This is the best of what has been said about this verse, concerning which the views of the scholars, the exegetes and the grammarians have been extremely confused, and the context of the verse guides to it. (وظنوا) is conjoined to (استيأسوا) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Qur'anic verb is (استيأس)], and (أن) together with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of (ظنوا). (كذبوا) is passive, that is: the nations thought that the messengers had been let down regarding the victory promised them. The clause (كذبوا) is the khabar of (أنهم).
(جاءَهُمْ نَصْرُنا فَنُجِّيَ مَنْ نَشاءُ): the clause (جاءهم) has no grammatical position, because it [Translator's note: the source has «لأنهم», "because they", evidently for «لأنها»] is the reply of (إذا). (جاءهم نصرنا) is a verb, a direct object and an agent. The fāʾ is a conjunction, and (نجي), passive, is conjoined to (جاءهم); (من) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and (نشاء) the ṣila.
(وَلا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنا عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction and (لا) negative; (يرد) is passive; (بأسنا) is the deputy agent; (عن القوم) is attached to (يرد); and (المجرمين) is an adjective.
(لَقَدْ كانَ فِي قَصَصِهِمْ عِبْرَةٌ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ): the lām is the reply to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realization; (في قصصهم) is a fronted predicate and (عبرة) a postponed subject; (لأولي) is an adjective of (عبرة), and (الألباب) the muḍāf ilayhi. The purport of this lesson will come in the section on rhetoric.
(ما كانَ حَدِيثاً يُفْتَرى): (ما) is negative; (كان) is a defective past verb whose noun is a latent pronoun referring to the Qur'an; (حديثا) is its predicate; and the clause (يفترى) is an adjective of (حديثا).
(وَلكِنْ تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لكن) is lightened and inoperative; (تصديق) is conjoined to (حديثا), which is preferable to supplying (كان) — the like of this has preceded in Sūrat Yūnus. (الذي) is the muḍāf ilayhi and the adverb is the ṣila. (تفصيل كل شيء) and (هدى) and (رحمة) are conjoined to (تصديق); (لقوم) is an adjective, and the clause (يؤمنون) is an adjective of (قوم).

* Rhetoric:
In Sūrat Yūsuf there is a breath of the splendid narrative that fulfils the conditions of the story as the researches of critics in the modern age have arrived at them, which may be taken from their many sources. This story, along with the sequence of its events, the abundance of its artistry and the variety of its chapters, is distinguished by concision (al-ījāz). We alluded to this earlier, and we expand on it here, saying:

1- The division of concision:
Concision comes in two kinds:
1- a long kind, 2- and a short kind.
The long kind is long relative to the short kind, not relative to other speech, as with all the stories of the Qur'an; and the best of them in this respect is the story of Yūsuf, for it came in both ways in a single sura: from His words «نحن نقض عليك أحسن القصص» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص»] to His words «وخروا له سجدا»; and it came in the abridged way in His words on the tongue of Yūsuf: «يا أبت هذا تأويل رؤياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا وقد أحسن بي إذ أخرجني من السجن وجاء بكم من البدو من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين اخوتي». So the Exalted first mentioned the story by way of elaboration, in detail, for one who had no share in the means of knowing it, and mentioned it at the end in abridged form, so that one who did not know it would know it in detail, and then when it came in summary he would recognise the allusions in it. He began it with His words «نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص» and closed it with His words «لقد كان في قصصهم عبرة لأولي الألباب». The point of taking a lesson from their stories is that these stories were recorded only so that a lesson might be drawn from them and the wisdom and purport be known.

2- Variation in the form of the word:
In His words «لأولي الألباب» there is an art to which the ancients gave the name just mentioned. It is to eloquence what the heart is to a human being, and it is subtle except to those whose natural gifts are pure and in whom the faculty of eloquence is abundant. By variation in the form of the word we mean transferring it from one shape to another — such as transferring it from one pattern to another, or from the form of a noun to the form of a verb or vice versa, or from the past to the future or vice versa, or from the singular to the dual or plural, or to the nisba, and so on — whereupon its ugliness turns into beauty and its beauty into ugliness. We shall give examples arranged in the order we have set out. Among transfers of a word from one form to another is the word «خود», which denotes a soft woman; if it is transferred to the form of a verb one says «خوّد» on the pattern faʿʿala, meaning "to hasten": one says «خوّد البعير» when the camel hastens. In the form of the noun it is fine and splendid, but when it comes in the form of the verb it is not considered good, as in the saying of Abū Tammām in an ode praising Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm:
وإلى بني عبد الكريم تواهقت ... رتك النعام رأى الظلام فخودا
(And towards the sons of ʿAbd al-Karīm [the camels] vied in pace — the trot of the ostrich that saw the darkness and sped.)
It is heavy and graceless, as you see; yet its heaviness and gracelessness lighten when it is transferred from literal to figurative use, as in the saying of a man of Banū Asad:
أقول لنفسي حين خود رألها ... رويدك لما تشفقي حين مشفق
رويدك حتى تنظري عمّ ينجلي ... غيابة هذا البارق المتألق
(I say to my soul when its ostrich-chick sped off: gently — do not fear yet, the time for fearing has not come; gently, until you see what the hidden depth of this gleaming lightning clears away to.)
Al-raʾl is the [young] ostrich, and what is meant here is that his soul fled and took fright, and he likened that to the haste of the ostrich in its flight and fright. Since he used it figuratively, some of the ugliness attaching to the word «خوّد» was lifted from it. This is perceived by sound taste and has no fixed rule. The difference is not hidden between this word as used here and as used in Abū Tammām's verse: in Abū Tammām's verse it came ugly and graceless [Translator's note: the source has «سجة», evidently a misprint for «سمجة»], while here it came middling. As for transferring a verb from one form to another, its example is the word «ودع», a triliteral past verb with no heaviness in it and no discord among its letters; yet the Arabs refrained from using it in the past form because of its gracelessness, whereas when transferred to the future or the imperative it is fine and eloquent. The imperative is as in His words «فذرهم يخوضوا ويلعبوا» [Translator's note: the author's example is of the synonymous verb «ذر»], and it came in the Qur'an only in that way. Its transfer to the future form is as in the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
تشقّكم بقناها كل سلهبة ... والضرب يأخذ منكم فوق ما يدع
(Every tall steed cleaves you with its spears, and the striking takes from you more than it leaves.)
Here it is the height of eloquence. For this reason the Arabs let the past of «يدع» and «يذر» die out, and they found graceless the saying of Abū al-ʿAtāhiya despite the beauty of its meaning:
أثروا فلم يدخلوا قبورهم ... شيئا من الثروة التي جمعوا
وكان ما قدموا لأنفسهم ... أعظم نفعا من الذي ودعوا
(They grew rich, yet took into their graves nothing of the wealth they had amassed; and what they had sent ahead for themselves was of greater benefit than what they left behind.)
As for transfer from the singular to the dual and plural, its example is the verse we are dealing with. The word «اللب» meaning the intellect — not «اللب» meaning what lies under the husk — is only good in usage in the plural, and so it came here and in more than one place in the Noble Qur'an. It may be used in the singular, but on condition that it is annexed (muḍāf) or annexed to (muḍāf ilayhi). Its being muḍāf is as in the saying of the Prophet ﷺ in mentioning women: «I have not seen any deficient in intellect and religion more able to carry off the mind (lubb) of a resolute man than one of you, O company of women». Its being muḍāf ilayhi is as in the saying of Jarīr:
إن العيون التي في طرفها حور ... قتلننا ثم لم يحيين قتلانا
يصر عن ذا اللب حتى لا حراك به ... وهن أضعف خلق الله إنسانا
(The eyes in whose glance there is a dark lustre have slain us and then not revived our slain; they fell the man of mind until he cannot stir, though they are the weakest of Allah's creatures.) [Translator's note: the source has «يصر عن»; the well-known wording is «يصرعن».]
This is a matter that almost bewilders the eloquent speaker. Listen to the word «الصوف» (wool): in the singular you find it graceless in usage. Abū Tammām used it and it came out insipid, and what increased its insipidity is that it came figuratively, attributed to time, where he says:
كانوا برود زمانهم فتصدعوا ... فكأنما لبس الزمان الصوفا
(They were the fine cloaks of their age, then they were scattered — as if time had put on wool.)
But it occurred in the Noble Qur'an in the plural, and lo, it is delightful and moving. The Exalted said: «وجعل لكم من جلود الأنعام بيوتا تستخفونها يوم ظعنكم ويوم إقامتكم ومن أصوافها وأوبارها وأشعارها أثاثا ومتاعا إلى حين».
The Arabs prevented pluralising maṣdars (verbal nouns) only for this reason, and the pivot of the matter is sound taste and musical sound, whose beauty cannot be fathomed or described. ʿAntara used a maṣdar in the plural and it came out graceless and despised; he said:
فإن يبرأ فلم أنفث عليه ... وإن يفقد فحق له الفقود
(If he recovers, it was not I who breathed a charm on him; and if he is lost, then loss is his due.)
His word «الفقود» is the plural of the maṣdar from faqada yafqidu faqdan, and the use of such a word is not acceptable. All of this goes back to sound taste — may Allah have mercy on Voltaire, who said: "Your taste is your teacher."
Since we have reached this stage of literary analysis, we must point to a splendid book, "Maʿānī al-Qur'an" by al-Farrāʾ. The method of the book rests on the following:
The book follows an innovative method: it deals with the verses of each sura in order, not confining itself to rare words but going beyond them to clarify the grammatical side and the i'rab in the verse, and it arrives at general theory, explaining its rules, principles, proofs, causes and effects. Then it speaks of simile, proverb, metonymy and figurative speech in general, then takes up metaphor (istiʿāra), one of the two kinds of figurative speech, and iltifāt. However, what is entirely new in al-Farrāʾ's book is that he paid attention to the phonetic pattern, the interconnection of words, the harmony of tone and the agreement of the verse-endings (fawāṣil) at the ends of verses. He allows the dropping of word-endings in agreement with the verse-endings, provided this agrees with the speech of the Arabs, as in His words «والليل إذا يسر»: "The readers read «يسري» with the yāʾ retained and «يسر» with it dropped, and dropping it is dearer to me because of its matching the verse-endings. The Arabs may drop the yāʾ and make do with the kasra of what precedes it. Someone recited to me:
كفاك كف ما تليق درهما ... جودا وأخرى تعط بالسيف الدما
(Your two hands: one hand that does not hold on to a dirham out of generosity, and another that gives blood with the sword.)
and another recited to me:
ليس يخفي يسارتي قدر يوم ... ولقد يخف شيمتي إعساري
(My ease does not hide my worth for a day, and my hardship may conceal my nature.)
And His words «بطغواها»: He meant "by its transgression (ṭughyān)", except that «الطغوى» better matches the verse-endings, so it was chosen for that reason. Do you not see that He said «وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله», meaning the last of their supplication (duʿāʾ), and likewise «دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم» — this is their supplication therein; and «وما قلى», meaning "nor does He hate you (qalāka)", the kāf being dropped, just as you say "I have given you and done well", meaning "done well to you", one being sufficient without repeating the other [Translator's note: the source has «فيكتفى بالياء الاولى», "one makes do with the first yāʾ"]; and because the verse-endings are in yāʾ, both factors came together in it." Until al-Farrāʾ says: "…and His words, Mighty and Majestic, «فأغنى» «فآوى» — He means by it "so He enriched you" and "sheltered you"; it proceeded on dropping the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the dropped element is the kāf] to match the verse-endings." [Translator's note: the word «لله» appearing before this quotation in the source seems to be stray.]
In his delightful book "Maʿānī al-Qur'an", al-Farrāʾ allows the annexation of a maṣdar to its owner, as in His words «إذا زلزلت الأرض زلزالها». He said:
"So the maṣdar was annexed to its owner, while you say in speech: 'I will surely give you your gift', meaning a gift; and what brought it near to permissibility was its agreement with the verse-endings that came after it."
In this way al-Farrāʾ set before us general rules for the changes that may occur in words, which the Qur'an sometimes resorts to for musical harmony in its composition, and the connection of those changes with what happens to the rhyme in poetry for the sake of the metre. Al-Farrāʾ never ceases to point out that the Qur'an, in turning from one word to another or modifying words, does not depart from the styles of the Arabs and their arts of speech, especially in poetry, which is metrical speech whose agreement and harmony in its composition resemble what the style of the Qur'an observes. Passages from al-Farrāʾ's book showing what distinguishes this great tome in several areas of eloquence will appear in scattered places in this book.
Al-Jāḥiẓ, in his book "Naẓm al-Qur'an", which he wrote for al-Fatḥ ibn Khāqān, the vizier of al-Mutawakkil ʿalā Allāh — which, alas, was never printed, but was lost along with the books lost in the ordeal of Baghdad inflicted upon it by Hülegü, only fragments of it surviving scattered in al-Jāḥiẓ's other printed books — holds that the Revelation gave the word special care, choosing it precisely to indicate the meanings precisely. Two words may share a meaning, but one is more precise than the other in indicating it. The composition of the Qur'an has its mastery in placing the word in its proper station in the place intended for it, and is distinguished also by its splendour in choice and in observing the differences between words: it does not bring synonymous words to indicate a single meaning, but to indicate different meanings. According to the precision with which the meaning is hit lies the difference between people's words in their speech and the words of the Qur'an. He says on this subject: "People may favour words and use them while others are more deserving of that. Do you not see that Allah the Exalted did not mention hunger (al-jūʿ) in the Qur'an except in the context of punishment or of abject poverty and evident incapacity? People do not mention saghab, and they mention jūʿ in states of ability and well-being. Likewise the mention of rain (al-maṭar): you do not find the Qur'an uttering it except in contexts of vengeance, whereas the common people and most of the elite do not distinguish between mentioning maṭar and mentioning ghayth. And the wording of the Qur'an upon which it was revealed is that when it mentions sights (abṣār) it does not say hearings (asmāʿ), and when it mentions seven heavens it does not say earths (araḍīn). Do you not see that it does not pluralise arḍ as araḍīn, nor samʿ as asmāʿ? What runs on the tongues of the common people is otherwise; they do not seek out among words the one most deserving of mention and most fitting for use. Some of the readers claimed that nikāḥ is not mentioned in the Qur'an except in the sense of marriage."
Al-Jāḥiẓ dealt with the tone, music and particular regular metre, made up of interconnected harmonious units, on which the composition of the Qur'an runs. How we wished this book had survived, so that we might enjoy its researches; but we shall try to gather what is scattered of it in this book. He addressed the metre of the Qur'an and spoke at length to deny that it has the metre of poetry. He says on this subject: "It is put to the one who attacked His words «تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب» and claimed that it is poetry because it scans as mustafʿilun mafāʿilun: it is said to him: know that if you examined people's conversations, sermons and letters you would find in them much like mustafʿilun mustafʿilun, and mustafʿilun fāʿilun, and no one on earth regards that amount as poetry. If a pedlar cried out: 'Who will buy aubergines?' he would have spoken words in the metre mustafʿilun mafʿūlātu. How can this be poetry when its speaker did not aim at poetry? This amount of metre may occur in all speech; but when the amount comes that is known to be the product of poetry, knowledge of metres and aiming at them, that is poetry. This is straightforward and the answer to it is easy, praise be to Allah."
Ibn Qutayba, in his book "Mushkil al-Qur'an", holds that the musical tone, the composition and the inner rhythm in the verses are one of the properties on which the inimitability of the Qur'an rests. It is sweet in tone, regular in cadence, its sound beloved to souls; ears do not tire of it because of the gentle music flowing through its expressions and among its words, and tongues do not stumble over it because of its smoothness. On this Ibn Qutayba says:
"And He made it recited over long recitation, and heard without the ears rejecting it, and fresh, not wearing out with much repetition."
We close this discussion — intending to return to it elsewhere — with a word that occurred in the Qur'an very beautifully and occurred in poetry and was flat, namely the word «يؤذي». Abū al-Ṭayyib said:
تلذ له المروءة وهي تؤذي ... ومن يعشق يلذ له الغرام
(Manliness is sweet to him though it causes hurt — and whoever loves, passion is sweet to him.)
This verse is beautiful and noble in meaning, except that the word «تؤذي» [Translator's note: the source writes «يؤذي» here] came in it insipid and flat, whereas it occurred in the Qur'an supremely splendid and evidently perfect, in His words: «فإذا طعمتم فانتشروا ولا مستأنسين لحديث إن ذلكم كان يؤذي النبي فيستحيي منكم والله لا يستحيي من الحق». It seems to us that it occurred in Abū al-Ṭayyib's verse cut off: do you not see that he said «تلذ له المروءة وهي تؤذي» and then said «ومن يعشق يلذ له الغرام», bringing a resumptive statement? This is a long subject, the probing of whose depth and the fathoming of whose beauty rest on sound taste and fine nature.
Further, one cannot avoid pointing out that most of the stories that occur in the Noble Qur'an are stories of the prophets in their struggle to convey their message, spread their call and resist their opponents among those in authority who rejected them and stood between them and the guidance of their peoples.
If the stories of the Noble Qur'an are examined carefully, it becomes clear to one who looks into their contents that their first lesson is lessons by which guides and those who call to reform may benefit, since among the social obligations of Islam is that a group from the community be appointed to call to good, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.
Among those lessons is that the ignorant submit to command and might and do not submit to argument and proof, and they want the one with the call — as came in the story of Nūḥ — to be an angel, or to have the treasuries of Allah, and they say to him: «قد جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين».
Among those lessons is that the masters [Translator's note: the source has «أصحاب السادة»; the sense is "those of lordship"] in the community dislike change and cling to the old, and they reproach the prophet for being followed by people who are not of lordship and rank: «وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادىء الرأي وما نرى لكم علينا من فضل بل نظنكم كذبين».
Among those lessons is that rigid adherence to inherited traditions is the greatest bane of the human intellect, for it paralyses its thinking and leaves it in the condition of a machine running on one track in the footsteps of fathers and forefathers despite the difference of times and the change of circumstances.
However, in the Noble Qur'an there are various stories other than stories of the call or stories of the struggle to convey the message, but they too are intended for their lesson and not for their historical reports. Among them is the story of Yūsuf with which we are dealing: it is the story of a human being who from his childhood was tried by the banes of human nature — from the envy of brothers, to the seduction of a woman, to the injustice of prison, to the burdens of office and the management of affairs at the height of hardship and famine.

dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْقَصَصِ): It has two possible analyses. The first is that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "relating" (iqtiṣāṣ); you say قصّ الحديث يقصّه قصصا ("he related the account, relating it"). The second is that it is a noun in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ūl), like النفض in the sense of المنفوض ("that which is shaken off"). Its derivation is from قصّ أثره ("he followed his trail") when he follows it, because the one who relates an account follows what he has memorized of it, little by little.

* I'rab:
(الر تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ) الر: its i'rab and what is said about it have already been given. تلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), آيات is the khabar (predicate), الكتاب is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and المبين is a naʿt (adjective) of الكتاب.
(إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ) inna and its noun; the clause أنزلناه is its khabar. قرآنا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in أنزلناه, that is, the ـه; it is also said that it is accusative as a badal (substitute) for the pronoun. عربيا is an adjective. And لعلكم تعقلون: la'alla and its noun, and the clause تعقلون is its khabar. (نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِما أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ هذَا الْقُرْآنَ) نحن is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause نقص is the khabar; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن". عليك is attached to نقص (mutaʿalliq). أحسن is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) if القصص is a maṣdar in the sense of the passive participle, and a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) if القصص is a maṣdar not meant in the sense of the passive participle. القصص is a muḍāf ilayhi. The بـ is causal, and ما is maṣdarī (forming a verbal noun); it, together with what follows it, is in the genitive through the بـ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to نقص, that is, "because of Our revealing". إليك is attached to أوحينا; هذا is a mafʿūl bihi, and القرآن is a badal from the demonstrative. (وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغافِلِينَ) The wāw is the wāw of ḥāl; إن is the lightened form of the heavy إنّ; كان and its noun; من قبله is a ḥāl; the lām is the discriminating lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); and من الغافلين is the khabar of كنت. (إِذْ قالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ: يا أَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً)
It is permissible for you to attach the adverbial إذ to an omitted verb, that is, "Remember" (اذكر); and it is permissible for you to make it a badal al-ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from أحسن القصص; and it is permissible to attach it to نقص, but in that there is a removal of إذ from the past sense. The clause قال يوسف is what the adverbial is annexed to; لأبيه is attached to قال; يا is a vocative particle; أبت is the one addressed, annexed to the first-person yāʾ, which was dropped and replaced by the kasra-vowelled or fatḥa-vowelled tāʾ (more on this will come in the section on Benefits). The hamza of إن is vowelled with kasra after the verb of saying; the yāʾ is the noun of إنّ and the clause رأيت is its khabar. أحد عشر are two numeral parts, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of رأيت; كوكبا is a tamyīz (specification). رأيت is from الرؤيا, that is, the dream, and it takes two objects. (وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي ساجِدِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; الشمس and القمر are conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أحد عشر كوكبا; رأيتهم is a verb, agent and direct object, and it is not an emphasis (tawkīd) of the first رأيتهم; لي is attached to ساجدين, and ساجدين is a second direct object of رأيتهم. Abū al-Baqāʾ gave it the i'rab of a ḥāl and said that the seeing is of the eye; the verification of this will come in the section on Rhetoric. (قالَ يا بُنَيَّ لا تَقْصُصْ رُؤْياكَ عَلى إِخْوَتِكَ) The i'rab of يا بني was given earlier in Hūd; لا is prohibitive; تقصص is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; رؤياك is a direct object; and على إخوتك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقصص. (فَيَكِيدُوا لَكَ كَيْداً إِنَّ الشَّيْطانَ لِلْإِنْسانِ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ) The فاء is causal (sababiyya), and يكيدوا is accusative by an implied أن, because it comes as the response to a prohibition; the wāw is the fāʿil; لك is attached to يكيدوا; كيدا may be an emphatic mafʿūl muṭlaq, and may be a mafʿūl bihi, that is, "they would contrive a plot against you". And إنّ الشيطان: inna and its noun; للإنسان is a ḥāl; عدو is the khabar of inna; and مبين is an adjective.
(وَكَذلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحادِيثِ) كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "Just as He chose you and selected you for this great vision, He will choose you for great matters"; the kāf is the object of يجتبيك; ربك is the fāʿil; and ويعلمك is not conjoined to يجتبيك but is a resumptive statement, as if it were said "and He will teach you and complete His favour"; من تأويل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يعلمك, and الأحاديث is a muḍāf ilayhi. (وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلى آلِ يَعْقُوبَ) It is conjoined to يعلمك; نعمته is a mafʿūl bihi; عليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نعمته or to يتم; and على آل يعقوب is conjoined to it. (كَما أَتَمَّها عَلى أَبَوَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْحاقَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ) كما: the كاف with ما is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "a completion like His completion of it upon your two forefathers"; على أبويك is attached to أتمها; من قبل is a ḥāl; إبراهيم is a badal from أبويك or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); إسحق is conjoined to إبراهيم; and inna with its noun and its two khabars.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying, the Exalted, «رأيتهم» there is a repetition which the observer at first glance thinks is an emphasis of the first, but it is not an emphasis; rather it is a resumptive statement, on the assumption of a question to which it came as the answer. It is also permissible for it to be for emphasis, on the grounds that the length of the interval caused by the objects called for it, so رأيتهم was brought in for freshness and for variety in the narration.
2- In His saying «ساجدين», He treated the eleven stars, the sun and the moon as rational beings, which the grammarians call taghlīb (giving precedence to the rational). This description is technical; as for the rhetorical secret, it is something hidden behind this description. That is because, when He described the stars, the sun and the moon with what is particular to rational beings, namely prostration, He applied to them their ruling, as though they were rational; this is frequent and widespread in their speech, and much of it will come in the Qur'an.
3- Barāʿat al-takhalluṣ (skilful transition):
It is a famous art, widespread in the speech of the eloquent. It is the blending of what the writer or poet puts forward by way of expansion with what he opened his speech with first, such as the first verse of a qaṣīda or the first paragraph of an essay, in that he slips this in with a graceful, subtle-meaning stealth, such that the listener does not notice the transition from the first meaning until he has already fallen into the second, because of the intensity of the blending and the cohesion, as though both had been poured into a single mould; or the writer prepares in it a section for a section he intends to bring after it, or by a point that indicates the meaning of the coming section, as in His saying, the Exalted: «نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص». For He, glory be to Him, prepared with this section for what comes after it, the recounting of the story of Yūsuf, peace be upon him, and so made a skilful transition by it to the mention of the story. The point that indicated the description of this story as being of the utmost beauty, unlike the rest of the stories of the prophets mentioned in the Qur'an, is His saying:
«أحسن القصص». For when the addressee's ear is struck by this description of the story, he is alerted to ponder it, and finds that every episode in it ended in good, every narrowness ended in ease, and every hardship turned to comfort. That is a wondrous matter, and it is impossible for the modern story to end its "knot" (al-ʿuqda) in good, or what is called in the convention of the modern story the "resolution":
1- Yūsuf was thrown into the well and his knot was tightened, then he was saved.
2- He was sold for the paltry price, which points in its meaning to lowliness and humiliation, and the knot tightened a second time, and behold, the one who bought him chose him and placed him with himself in the position of a son.
3- She in whose house he was solicited him for himself, desire leapt up, pleasure cried out, and reason almost snapped and right guidance almost departed, and the knot tightened a third time, and behold, he reined in the unruliness of his soul and held himself back.
4- He entered the prison, its darkness settled on him and its landmarks grew dim, and the knot tightened a fourth time, and he came out of it a king.
5- He gained the upper hand over his brothers after he had come to know their treachery toward him and their attempt to destroy him, yet he did not go with the whim of the soul that seeks revenge and retaliation, and he calmed his excess.
6- Allah gladdened him with the meeting with his full brother after despair, and he found companionship in him.
7- His father was separated from him and grieved for him until he went blind, and the knot tightened another time; then he was reunited with him, was gladdened by meeting him, and the father returned seeing.
8- Allah brought him from the desert and settled him in Egypt on the throne of kingship.
9- He and his father were angry with the rest of the sons, then were pleased with them.
10- Then, finally, his parents and his brothers prostrated to him, fulfilling his vision, so the ending matched the beginning, and the skilful transition was among the most beautiful things known in writing.

Husn al-takhalluṣ (beautiful transition) in poetry:
However, we must not fail to cite some of what has come of beautiful transition in our Arabic poetry, and it is regrettable that it generally ends in praise; we do not approve of this praise nor acknowledge it, except insofar as it is pure convention or a record of the general benefit that came at the hands of the one praised. Abū Tammām said, praising Abū Dulaf, an Arab hero famous for his jihad:
ودع فؤادك توديع الفراق فما ... أراه من سفر التوديع منصرفا
يجاذب الشوق طورا ثم يجذبه ... جهاده للقوافي في أبي دلفا
(Bid your heart farewell with the farewell of parting, for I do not see it turning away from the journey of farewell; longing pulls at it at times, then his striving for the rhymes pulls it, in Abū Dulaf.) «[Translator's note: the second verse is given in the source in a corrupted form; it is translated here as written.]»
Among the most delicate transitions is the saying of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī:
ولو أن المطيّ لها عقول ... وجدك لم تشد لها عقالا مواصلة لها رحلي كأني ... من الدنيا أريد بها ان
فصالا سألن فقلت مقصدنا سعيد ... فكان اسم الأمير لهن فالا
(If the riding camels had minds, by your good fortune you would not have tied a hobble on them ... [the rest is garbled]; they asked, and I said: "Our destination is Saʿīd," and the name of the Emir was an omen for them.) «[Translator's note: the verses are run together and corrupted in the source (the first verse is joined to words from another verse, and the line break falls mid-sentence), so only the sense that can be made out is rendered in the gloss.]»

* Benefits:
1- «رأى» from الرؤيا (the dream):
The grammarians and lexicographers differed about the dream-sense «رأى»; the verifiers hold that it is attached to the knowledge-sense رأى in taking two objects, on the common ground of perception by the inner sense, as in His saying, the Exalted: «إني أراني أعصر خمرا»: أرى operated on two attached pronouns referring to one referent, one of them the fāʿil and the second the first object, and the clause أعصر خمرا is the second object. And like the saying of ʿAmr ibn Aḥmar al-Bāhilī, mentioning a group of his people who had joined Syria, and he saw them in his sleep:
أراهم رفقتي حتى إذا ما ... تجافى الليل وانخزل انخزالا
(I saw them as my companions, until when the night drew away and slipped off completely.) The ـهم is the first object and رفقتي, with ḍamma or kasra on the rāʾ, is the second object. The vision here is a dream, by the evidence of his saying: حتى إذا ما تجافى الليل وانخزل انخزالا, that is, it was folded up and cut off. To this Ibn Mālik pointed in the Khulāṣa:
ولرأى الرؤيا الم ما لعلما ... طالب مفعولين من قبل انتمى
(For "raʾā" of the dream, what is for "ʿalima" ... seeking two objects, as stated before.) «[Translator's note: the second hemistich is garbled in the source; it is rendered as written.]»
Some went to the view that the dream-sense رأى does not take two objects, and that the second of the two accusatives is a ḥāl; this was rejected because it occurs here as a definite noun, and it was objected that الرفقة, being those who associate and accompany, has the sense of the active participle, so the annexation in it is not a true (maḥḍa) annexation. «[Translator's note: the source also repeats, in garbled form, the first words of this passage ("وذهب بعضهم إلى أن رأى الحلمية لا تنصب مفعولين من قبل انتمى"), and a stray repetition of the Khulāṣa hemistich; the repeated fragment is rendered once here.]»
2- The report of the Jew and Yūsuf's stars:
We see it as useful to draw attention to the reports the exegetes relate about Yūsuf's stars. Al-Ḥākim in his Mustadrak recorded that a Jew came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Tell me the names of the stars that Yūsuf, peace be upon him, saw." He said: "If I tell you their names, will you become Muslim?" He said: "Yes."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "al-Dhayyāl, al-Wathāb, al-Ṭāriq, al-Faylaq, al-Ṣubḥ, al-Qābis, al-Ḍarūḥ, al-Kharthān, al-Katifān, al-ʿAmūdān and Dhū al-Farʿ." He said:
"You have spoken truly, O Muḥammad," but he did not become Muslim. The fabrication of this report is evident, and in its chain of transmission are a group who have been criticized. Ibn al-Jawzī said: it is fabricated.

dervis-irab:50-53.t:
* Vocabulary:
(خَطْبُكُنَّ): your affair. It is originally the verbal noun of خطب يخطب, but it is used only of grave matters. In al-Mukhtār: "al-khaṭb is the matter; you say: ما خطبك, and al-Azharī said, that is, what is your matter; and you say هذا خطب جليل (this is a grave matter) and خطب يسير (a slight matter); its plural is khuṭūb." In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: al-khaṭb is a verbal noun meaning the affair; one says ما خطبك؟, that is, what is your affair and what moved you to it; its use has come to predominate for a grave, disagreeable matter.
(حَصْحَصَ): that is, it became firm and settled. al-Khalīl said: حصحص means it became clear and manifest after having been hidden. Some said it is derived from al-ḥiṣṣa (the share), the meaning being that the share of truth became distinct from the share of falsehood, just as the shares of lands and the like are distinguished. al-Rāghib said: حصحص الحق is the uncovering of what had been submerging it; ḥaṣṣa and ḥaṣḥaṣa are like kaffa and kafkafa; ḥaṣṣahu means he cut it, either by direct action or by judgement; al-ḥiṣṣa is a portion of the whole and is used in the sense of "share". In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: it is from ḥaṣḥaṣa al-baʿīr, when the camel lets its thafanāt (callosities) down to kneel. He said:
فحصحص في صم الصفا ثفناته ... وناء بسلمى نوءة ثم صمما
(He pressed his callosities into the hard rock, and rose with Salmā, then pressed on.)
The thafanāt are those parts of the camel that touch the ground when it kneels and that are thick, such as the knees and the like. It was also said that it is from al-ḥaṣṣ, which is the falling out of hair so that what is beneath becomes clear; the second ḥāʾ is a substitute for a third ṣād. When identical letters occur together in such a word, the Arabs substitute for the middle letter a letter of the preceding kind; likewise ḥathḥathtu and raqraqtu, whose origins are ḥathathtu and raqaqtu. This is the view of the Kufans. The Basrans said that they are two dialectal forms that came close to each other, since a letter is substituted only for its like or for a letter close to it in point of articulation, and these letters are far apart, so substituting them is not valid.

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ فَلَمَّا جاءَهُ الرَّسُولُ): conjoined to an omitted clause, that is, "when the messenger came to him and informed him of its interpretation, the king said". The clause ائتوني به is the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl). فلما: the فاء is a conjunction, and لما is a temporal adverbial particle, or a connective. جاءه الرسول: a verb, a fronted direct object (mafʿūl bihi), and an agent (fāʿil).
(قالَ ارْجِعْ إِلى رَبِّكَ فَسْئَلْهُ ما بالُ النِّسْوَةِ اللَّاتِي قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ): he paved the way for the interpretation of the dream by asking about the women, so that his innocence of what he had been accused of, and imprisoned for, would become manifest. In the hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: "I marvelled at Yūsuf, his generosity and his patience, may Allah forgive him, when he was asked about the lean and the fat cows; had I been in his place I would not have told them until I had stipulated that they release me." ارجع: an imperative verb whose agent is the latent pronoun "you". إلى ربك: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ارجع. فاسأله: conjoined to ارجع; the هاء is a direct object. ما: an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject). بال: a khabar (predicate). The clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of اسأله, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from operating by the interrogative. النسوة: a muḍāf ilayhi of بال. اللاتي: a relative, an adjective. The clause قطعن أيديهن is the ṣila (relative clause).
(إِنَّ رَبِّي بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِيمٌ): inna and its subject; بكيدهن is attached to عليم, and عليم is the khabar of inna.
(قالَ ما خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ راوَدْتُنَّ يُوسُفَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ): ما: an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ. خطبكن: the khabar. إذ: an adverb attached to خطبكن because it carries the sense of a verb, the meaning being "what did you do, and what did you want of him at that time?" The clause راودتن is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. راودتن: a verb and an agent. يوسف: a direct object. عن نفسه: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to راودتن.
(قُلْنَ حاشَ لِلَّهِ ما عَلِمْنا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ سُوءٍ): حاش: what was said about it has already preceded, that is, in exalting Him above being described as incapable of creating a chaste human being such as this one. لله: explicative (bayān). ما: negative. علمنا: a verb and an agent. عليه: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to علمنا. من: a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. سوء: genitive in form through من, accusative in position as the object of علمنا.
(قالَتِ امْرَأَةُ الْعَزِيزِ الْآنَ حَصْحَصَ الْحَقُّ): قالت امرأة العزيز: a verb and an agent. الآن: an adverb of time attached to حصحص. الحق: the agent of حصحص.
(أَنَا راوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ): أنا: a mubtadaʾ. The clause راودته is the khabar; it consists of a verb, an agent and a direct object. عن نفسه: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to راودته. The واو is a conjunction. إن and its subject; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); من الصادقين is the khabar of إنه.
(ذلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِالْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي كَيْدَ الْخائِنِينَ): the exegetes differed over who spoke these words, and it is hard to decide the matter or to prefer one view, so let us give both opinions. Some said: it is Yūsuf's speech, that is, "that tucking up of my skirts and that firmness was so that his innocence would appear, so that the ʿAzīz might know that I did not betray him." al-Farrāʾ said: it is not implausible that the speech of one person be joined to the speech of another when the indication that distinguishes each of them points to what is fitting for it; and the allusion is to the incident that took place on his part, namely his deliberation and patience. Others said it is the speech of Zulaykhāʾ [Translator's note: the source spells the name Zanīkhāʾ (زنيخاء)], the meaning being "that which I said was so that Yūsuf might know that I did not betray him." Whatever the case, ذلك is a mubtadaʾ; ليعلم: the lām is for causation, and يعلم is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the lām of causation, and the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar. It is also permissible that these words be meant for general circumstances, in which case ذلك is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "the matter is that". أن and what follows it are in the interpretation of a maṣdar that takes the place of the two objects of يعلم. The clause لم أخنه is the khabar of أني. بالغيب is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent or the object; it may also be an adverbial, that is, "in the place of the unseen," attached to أخنه. وأن الله: conjoined to أني. The clause لا يهدي is the khabar of أن. كيد الخائنين: a direct object.
(وَما أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ إِلَّا ما رَحِمَ رَبِّي): the واو is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ما: negative. أبرئ نفسي: an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object. إن النفس: inna and its subject; the shifted lām; أمارة بالسوء is its khabar. إلا: a particle of exception. ما may be maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), its position being accusative, the implied sense being "the soul is indeed prone to command evil, except to whom my Lord has shown mercy," its accusative being adverbial; and ما may be in the sense of من, the implied sense being "the soul commands evil, except for the one on whom my Lord has had mercy," or "except a soul on which my Lord has had mercy, for it does not command evil." Abū Ḥayyān's wording is: "The apparent sense is that إلا ما رحم ربي is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) from his words لأمارة بالسوء, because by his words إن النفس he intended the genus, as though he said: except the soul on which my Lord has had mercy, which then does not command evil; so it is an exception from the latent pronoun in أمارة. It is also possible that it is excepted from the omitted object of أمارة, as the implied sense is 'it is prone to command its owner to evil, except the one on whom my Lord has had mercy, for it does not command him to evil.' They also allowed that it be excepted from an adverb of time whose generality is understood from what precedes the exception, with ما temporal (ẓarfiyya), as the implied sense is 'prone to command evil for as long as it lasts, except at the time of Allah's mercy to the servant and His taking it away from the desire for acts of disobedience.' They also allowed that it be a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ) with ما maṣdar-forming, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned that it is the view of the majority, that is, 'but the mercy of my Lord is what turns away wrongdoing.'"
(إِنَّ رَبِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): inna and its subject and its two khabars.

* Rhetoric:
The rhetoricians preferred that the words "ذلك ليعلم ..." be the speech of Zulaykhā, because it is closer to the situation and more fitting to the register of love-talk, where the lover ransoms the beloved with herself. Do you not see that when the ordeal grew severe and reached its extreme she ransomed him with herself and said: (الْآنَ حَصْحَصَ الْحَقُّ أَنَا راوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ), and drew near to his heart by her words "ذلك ليعلم اني لم أخنه بالغيب"? How fine is the saying of Kuthayyir, who glanced at the heaven of this meaning, in drawing near to the beloved and captivating his heart with such gentleness:
يود بأن يمسي عليلا لعلها ... إذا سمعت شكواه يوما تراسله
ويهتز للمعروف في طلب العلا ... لتحمد يوما عند ليلى شمائله
(He wishes to spend the evening ill, so that perhaps she, when she hears his complaint one day, will send word to him. / And he is moved to kindness in his quest for eminence, so that his qualities may one day be praised in Laylā's presence.)
That is also confirmed by her words to the women whose scheming she had heard of: "فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه," unconcerned about what they had exposed her with. Jamīl ibn Maʿmar al-Khuzāʿī also glanced at this lofty heaven and said:
وماذا عسى الواشون أن يتحدثوا ... سوى أن يقولوا: إنني لك عاشق
أجل صدق الواشون أنت حبيبة ... إليّ وإن لم تصف منك الخلائق
(What can the slanderers say, other than that they say: "I am your lover"? Yes, the slanderers have spoken truly: you are beloved to me, even if your natures are not pure.)
The author of al-Aghānī transmitted both verses as belonging to Majnūn Banī ʿĀmir.
ʿAmr ibn Ḍubayʿa al-Raqāshī, one of Banū Raqāsh, who are named after their mother, said:
ألا ليقل من شاء ما شاء إنما ... يلام الفتى فيما استطاع من الأمر
قضى الله حب المالكية فاصطبر ... عليه فقد تجري الأمور على قدر
(Let whoever wishes say what he wishes; a young man is blamed only for what he was able to do. Allah decreed love for al-Mālikiyya, so be patient in it, for matters run according to a decree.)
Abū l-ʿAtāhiya glanced at the two verses of Jamīl and said:
قال لي أحمد ولم يدر ما بي ... أتحب الغداة عتبة حقا
فتنفست ثم قلت نعم حبا ... جرى في العروق عرقا فعرقا
(Aḥmad said to me, not knowing what was in me: "Do you truly love ʿUtba this morning?" I sighed, then said: "Yes, a love that has run through my veins, vein after vein.")
And he surpassed him with this sigh, which every subtle soul follows.

* Benefits:
الآن:
al-Āna is one of the adverbs of time; its meaning is the present time, and it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. There is a difficulty over the reason for its indeclinability. One group held that it is indeclinable because it occurred, at the very first of its states, as a definite noun through the article (alif and lām), whereas the rule for nouns is that they be indefinite and common to the genus, and then something is added to them that makes them definite, such as annexation or the article. Since it differed from its sister nouns by occurring as definite from the first of its states and by keeping to a single place, it was made indeclinable on that account, because its keeping to this place made it resemble the particles. This is the view of Abū l-ʿAbbās al-Mubarrad, and al-Zamakhsharī and others followed him. al-Farrāʾ said: its origin is آن, from آن الشيء يئين when its time has come; one says آن لك أن تفعل كذا and أنى لك. ʿAmr ibn Ḥassān said:
تمخضت المنون له بيوم ... أنى ولكل حاملة تمام
(Fate went into labour for him with a day that had come; and every pregnant one has her term.)
آن is a past verb; when the article was added to it, it was left as it was, with the fatḥa, just as it came in the hadith that the Prophet ﷺ "forbade qīla wa-qāla" (gossip), and qīla and qāla are two past verbs to which the preposition was attached and which were left as they were. There are other explanations that we have passed over, since there is nothing of use in them.

dervis-irab:54-57.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِي): conjoined to what precedes. قال الملك: a verb and an agent. The clause ائتوني به is the quoted speech. استخلصه: a jussive imperfect verb, because it occurs as the answer to an imperative. al-istikhlāṣ is the purification of a thing from the impurities of partnership. He said that because Yūsuf was precious, and it is the habit of kings to make precious things pure for themselves to the exclusion of others.
(فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ قالَ إِنَّكَ الْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ): the فاء is conjoined to an omitted clause that can be implied as the course and events of the story accord with, that is, "the messenger came to Yūsuf and said: 'Answer the king,' so he rose, bidding farewell to the people of the prison and praying for them, for he had been their refuge and the place of their trust; then he put on his clothes and entered upon the king, and when ..." and so on. لما is a temporal adverbial particle, or a connective. كلمه: a verb, a latent agent and a direct object. The clause قال is the answer to لما and has no grammatical position. إن and its subject; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); لدينا is attached to مكين; مكين is the khabar of إن, and أمين is a second khabar.
(قالَ اجْعَلْنِي عَلى خَزائِنِ الْأَرْضِ إِنِّي حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ): اجعلني: an imperative verb; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), the agent is latent, its implied form being "you", and the yāʾ is a direct object. على خزائن الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the second object, that is, "a steward over the storehouses of the land". إن and its subject; حفيظ is its khabar and عليم its second khabar.
(وَكَذلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْها حَيْثُ يَشاءُ): وكذلك: an adjective of an omitted absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), that is, "and in the likeness of that manifest establishment We established". مكنا: a verb and an agent. The lām is attached to مكنا. The object of مكنا is omitted, that is, "matters". في الأرض: a ḥāl. The clause يتبوأ is a circumstantial clause from Yūsuf. منها: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتبوأ. حيث: an adverb of يتبوأ, or a direct object of it. The clause يشاء is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. The rest of the story, which the flow of the discourse required to be omitted, must be pointed out, that is: he appointed him in the place of the ʿAzīz; then Qiṭfīr, the ʿAzīz of Egypt, perished, and after his death the king married Yūsuf to the wife of the ʿAzīz. It was a surprise that combined delight and astonishment when Yūsuf entered upon her and said to her: "Is this not better than what you wanted?" She said: "O truthful one, do not blame me, for I was a naive, beautiful, simple woman, and my husband did not go to women, and I was, in the matter of handsomeness and beauty, as you are; so my soul overcame me, and Allah protected you" — to the end of that wonderful story, which fulfilled all the elements of a tale. Then he took hold of the reins of affairs, and near and far submitted to him.
(نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنا مَنْ نَشاءُ وَلا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to describe the just disposal that Allah the Exalted reserved to Himself. نصيب: an imperfect nominative verb, and the agent is "We". برحمتنا: attached to نصيب. من: a direct object. The clause نشاء is a ṣila. ولا نضيع: conjoined to نصيب. أجر المحسنين: a direct object.
(وَلَأَجْرُ الْآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَكانُوا يَتَّقُونَ): the lām is the lām of initiation (ibtidāʾ). أجر: a mubtadaʾ. الآخرة: a muḍāf ilayhi. خير: the khabar of أجر. للذين: attached to خير. The clause آمنوا is a ṣila. وكانوا: kāna and its subject; the clause يتقون is its khabar.

* Benefits:
The narrators of biographies wove incidents around this wonderful story, spun from imagination, and fabricated reports on which falsehood is evident because of their triviality and weakness, or their impossibility and contradiction of reason. So a person must scrutinise these reports on which fabrication is evident, condemn relying on them, and charge those who transmitted these additions with falsehood; and that is the way of the purveyors of falsehood in every sect.

dervis-irab:87-92.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَتَحَسَّسُوا): taḥassus is seeking good by means of the sense (ḥāssa), and it is close to tajassus with a jīm. It was also said: taḥassus with a ḥāʾ is used for good and with a jīm for evil, and from it comes al-jāsūs (the spy), who seeks to uncover people's private faults. This root has wonderful properties: it takes in all the stirrings of people and the whispers of their souls, and it points to producing an effect on things. One says: ḥassahu yaḥussuhu (of the pattern naṣara) meaning he killed it and uprooted it; ḥassa the animal means he shook the dust off it with the currying comb; the cold ḥassa the crops means it burned them; ḥassa the meat means he put it on the embers; ḥassa the fire means he returned it to the bread of the baking-pit and the roast from its sides so that it would be cooked; ḥassa yaḥissu ḥissan (of the pattern taʿiba) a thing or by a thing means he knew it, felt it and perceived it; ḥassa yaḥissu (of the two patterns taʿiba and jalasa) bi-l-khayr means he was certain of it; ḥassa li-fulān means he softened toward so-and-so; taḥassasa means he listened and looked; taḥassasa the news means he strove to find it out; taḥassasa a thing means he sought to learn about it and looked for it by means of the sense; taḥassasa minhu means he inquired into news of him. Al-ḥāssa is the feminine of al-ḥāss, and is the perceiving faculty of the soul; the five senses are hearing, sight, smell, taste and touch. The "ḥawāss of the land" are five: the cold, the hail, the wind, the locusts and the livestock, taken from ḥassa al-zarʿ (to destroy the crops). One says: "ḥawāss passed over the people", i.e., severe years. Al-ḥasīs is a faint sound, a movement, and a slain man. Ḥisās al-ḥummā (with kasra) is its touch and the first of its onset. Al-ḥissī is what is perceived by outward sensation, the opposite of the intellectual (ʿaqlī). As for the root j-s-s, it resembles it in a strange way: one says jassahu yajussuhu (of the pattern naṣara) and ijtassahu, meaning he touched it with his hand to get to know it; jassa the ground means he trod on it; jassahu bi-ʿaynihi means he sharpened his gaze at it to make it out; jassa, tajassasa and ijtassa the news and matters means he searched into them; al-jāss, plural jawāsīs, and al-jassās is the one who brings news; jawāss of a person are his five senses, the singular being jāssa; al-mijass and al-mijassa is the place of touch. Dūqala said:
ولها هن بض ملاذهن ... رابي المجسّة حشوه وقد
(Poetry as in the source.) [Translator's note: the verse is garbled in the source text and its meaning is not clear; it is reproduced as printed.] And "so-and-so is ḍayyiq al-mijass and al-mijassa" means not broad of chest; and al-mijassa is also the place the physician feels.
(مُزْجاةٍ): merchandise that is pushed away, which every merchant pushes away out of disinclination toward it and contempt for it, from azjaytuhu when you push it away and drive it off; and "the wind tazjī the clouds". In al-Miṣbāḥ: zajjaytuhu, with doubling, means I pushed it gently; "the wind tazjī the clouds" means it drives them with a gentle driving. One says azjāhu on the pattern of arḍāhu, and zajjāhu with doubling like zakkāhu. In al-Qāmūs: zajjāhu means he drove it and pushed it.
(تَثْرِيبَ): reproach. In al-Miṣbāḥ: tharraba ʿalayhi yatharribu (of the pattern ḍaraba) means he reproached and blamed; and by the imperfect with a yāʾ of the third person (Yathrib) a man of the ʿAmālīq was named, who built the city of the Prophet ﷺ, and so Madīna was named after him; al-Suhaylī said this. Tharrab with doubling is for intensity and multiplication, and from it comes the saying of the Exalted «لا تثريب عليكم اليوم». Al-tharb, on the pattern of fals, is the thin fat over the paunch and the intestines. Al-Rāzī said: al-tathrīb is reviling and going to the limit in blame. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The origin of tathrīb is from al-tharb, which is the fat that covers the paunch, and its meaning is the removal of the tharb, just as tajlīd and taqrīʿ mean removal of the skin (jild) and the scalp (qarʿ), because when it is gone that is the extreme of leanness and emaciation beyond which there is nothing; so it was made a figure for the rebuke that tears the honour to shreds and removes the 'water of the face' (dignity)."

* I'rab:
(يا بَنِيَّ اذْهَبُوا فَتَحَسَّسُوا مِنْ يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ) The i'rab of يا بني has already been given; اذهبوا is an imperative verb and agent; the fāʾ is a conjunction; تحسسوا is an imperative verb and agent; ومن يوسف is attached to تحسسوا; وأخيه is conjoined to يوسف. (وَلا تَيْأَسُوا مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, تيئسوا is jussive by لا and the wāw is the agent; ومن روح الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it. The discussion of this metaphor will come in the section of Rhetoric. (إِنَّهُ لا يَيْأَسُ مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْكافِرُونَ) إن and its ism; the clause لا ييئس is its khabar; ومن روح الله is attached to ييئس; إلا is a particle of restriction; القوم is the agent and الكافرون an adjective. (فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ) There is omission and abbreviation in it; the implied form is "so they left their father heading for Egypt, and when …" and so on. The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is a temporal adverbial particle or a connective; دخلوا is a verb and agent; وعليه is attached to دخلوا. (قالُوا يا أَيُّهَا الْعَزِيزُ مَسَّنا وَأَهْلَنَا الضُّرُّ) The clause قالوا has no position; ويا أيها العزيز is a vocative whose i'rab has already been given, and العزيز is a badal (substitute) of أي; مسنا is a verb and direct object; وأهلنا is conjoined to نا or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); and الضر is the agent. (وَجِئْنا بِبِضاعَةٍ مُزْجاةٍ فَأَوْفِ لَنَا الْكَيْلَ) The wāw is a conjunction; جئنا is a verb and agent; وببضاعة is attached to جئنا; and مزجاة is an adjective; فأوف: the fāʾ is a conjunction, أوف is an imperative verb, ولنا is attached to أوف, and الكيل is a direct object. (وَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْنا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْزِي الْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ) وتصدق is conjoined to فأوف; وعلينا is attached to تصدق; إن and its ism; the clause يجزي is its khabar; and المتصدقين is a direct object. (قالَ: هَلْ عَلِمْتُمْ ما فَعَلْتُمْ بِيُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ إِذْ أَنْتُمْ جاهِلُونَ) هل is an interrogative particle; علمتم is a verb and agent; ما is a relative noun, direct object, and it may be a maṣdar particle, i.e., "your deed with Yūsuf"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to فعلتم; وأخيه is conjoined to يوسف; إذ is an adverb attached to فعلتم, i.e., "you did that at the time of your ignorance"; وأنتم is a mubtadaʾ and جاهلون its khabar, the nominal clause being the one to which the adverb is annexed. The interrogative conveys magnification and awe, i.e., the deed you committed was of a kind that no one would venture upon it, but you ventured upon it heedless of the consequences and not knowing what the affair of Yūsuf would come to, from deliverance from the well and then the governorship of the king. The text of Yaʿqūb's letter which they presented to him will come in the section of Benefits. (قالُوا أَإِنَّكَ لَأَنْتَ يُوسُفُ) قالوا is a verb and agent; أإنك: the hamza is for confirmatory interrogation; إن and its ism; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); أنت is a mubtadaʾ and يوسف a khabar, and the clause is the khabar of إن. It is permissible that the pronoun أنت be a separating pronoun, as has already been given. (قالَ: أَنَا يُوسُفُ وَهذا أَخِي قَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا) أنا is a mubtadaʾ and يوسف a khabar. He spelled out the name and said "I am Yūsuf" to magnify what had befallen him of the wrong done by his brothers, as if he said: I am the one wronged, from whom what is forbidden was made lawful, whom they wanted to kill. وهذا is a mubtadaʾ and أخي the khabar; قد is a particle of affirmation; من is a past verb; الله is the agent; وعلينا is attached to من; and the clause is a ḥāl. (إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَتَّقِ وَيَصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) إن and its ism, which is the pronoun of the matter and situation (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); من is a conditional noun that jusses, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يتق is the protasis, jussive, its sign of jussive being the omission of the weak letter; ويصبر is conjoined to it; فإنه: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and إن and its ism; the clause لا يضيع is its khabar; and أجر المحسنين is a direct object; the protasis and its apodosis form the khabar of إن.
(قالُوا تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ آثَرَكَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا) The tāʾ is the tāʾ of oath and the Majestic Name is genitive by it; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "we swear"; the lām is the answer to the oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; آثرك الله is a verb, direct object and agent; وعلينا is attached to آثرك. (وَإِنْ كُنَّا لَخاطِئِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is lightened from the heavy إن and not operative; كان and its ism; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); and خاطئين is the khabar of كنا. (قالَ لا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ) The clause لا تثريب is the quoted speech; لا is the lā of generic negation and تثريب its ism and عليكم its khabar; واليوم is an adverb attached to an omitted second khabar or to what the khabar is attached to, namely عليكم; and in any case one pauses at it. It is not permissible to attach the adverb to the maṣdar, i.e., al-tathrīb, because it would then resemble a muḍāf, and whenever that is so it is declined and takes tanwīn, as in "lā khayran min Zaydin ʿindaka". It is surprising of al-Zamakhsharī that he allowed attaching the adverb to al-tathrīb; it is a slip, and I do not know how it occurred in him. From another side, it would also separate it from its dependent by the phrase «عليكم». It is permissible to attach the adverb to the verb that follows it. (يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ) An invocatory clause serving as a justification; يغفر الله is a verb and agent; ولكم is attached to يغفر; وهو is a mubtadaʾ and أرحم الراحمين a khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The metaphor of rawḥ for mercy. Its clarification is that al-rawḥ is a maṣdar meaning mercy, and its origin is the heart's repose from its distress. The meaning is: do not despair of a relief that comes to you from Allah.

* Benefits:
History relates that when Yūsuf's brothers said to Yūsuf «مسنا وأهلنا الضر» and humbled themselves before him, his eyes streamed with tears. It was also said that they handed him the letter of Yaʿqūb, and this is its text, which we record for the burning emotion and overflowing feeling in it:
"From Yaʿqūb Isrāʾīl Allah, son of Isḥāq the sacrificial offering of Allah, son of Ibrāhīm the friend of Allah, to the ʿAzīz of Egypt. To proceed: we are a household which trials have been assigned to. As for my grandfather, his hands and feet were bound and he was thrown into the fire to be burned, and Allah made it cool and safe for him. As for my father, the knife was put to his nape to slaughter him, and Allah ransomed him. As for me, I had a son who was the dearest of my children to me; his brothers took him to the wilderness, then came to me with his shirt smeared with blood and said, 'The wolf has eaten him', and my eyes went from weeping for him. Then I had a son who was his full brother on his mother's side, and I used to find consolation in him; they took him away, then came back and said that he had stolen and that you had detained him. We are a household that does not steal and does not beget a thief. So if you return him to me, well; if not, I shall call down upon you a curse that will reach the seventh of your descendants. Peace."
When Yūsuf read the letter he could not contain himself and his patience gave out. And even supposing the letter is not authentic, the breath of emotion in it calls for its being recorded.

dervis-irab:30-33.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نِسْوَةٌ): a group of women, said to be five. نسوة is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own wording, only from its meaning, which is امرأة ("woman"). Its feminine gender is not real but is by consideration of the group, and for that reason the feminine tāʾ was not attached to its verb. The well-known pronunciation has kasra on its nūn, and damma is permitted in one dialect and was actually read so. In al-Qāmūs and its commentary there is what suggests that النسوة (with kasra), النسوة (with damma), النساء, النسوان, النّسون and النسنين are all plurals of "woman" not from her own wording. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "نسوة is a singular noun for the plural of 'woman', and its feminine gender is not real, and for that reason the feminine tāʾ was not attached to its verb."
(شَغَفَها): her love entered the shaghāf of his heart. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "شغف الهوى قلبه شغفا (of the pattern نفع), and the noun is الشغف with two fatḥas; it reached his shaghāf, with fatḥa, which is the membrane around his heart. And شغفه المال means wealth was made attractive to him, so he loved it, and he is مشغوف به." The shaghāf is the veil of the heart; it is also said to be a thin skin called "the tongue of the heart". Al-Nābigha said:
وقد حال هم دون ذلك والحج ... مكان الشغاف تبتغيه الأصابع
(A worry came between that and it, and the pain was in the place of the shaghāf, which the fingers seek.)
(أَعْتَدَتْ): she prepared and made ready. اعتده له means "he prepared it for him", and عتيد means "prepared, present"; from it comes العتيدة, in which perfume and oils are kept.
(مُتَّكَأً): what they lean on, of cushions they rest against, after the custom of the arrogant in eating fruit, where the eater reclines on pillows and eats it with knives. It is also said that food such as citron and banana was called متكأ because one leans on cushions while eating it; so it is a mursal metaphor (majāz mursal) whose connection is proximity, or an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya).
(أَكْبَرْنَهُ): they magnified him, were awed by his dazzling beauty and his captivating, enthralling loveliness, and amazement overcame them. It is also said: أكبرن means "they menstruated", and the هاء is the hāʾ of pause. One says أكبرت المرأة when she menstruates; in reality it means she entered "greatness" (kibar), because when she menstruates she leaves the limit of youth for the limit of maturity. It is as if Abū al-Ṭayyib had glanced at this interpretation, and said, playfully and in amatory vein:
خف الله واستر ذا الجمال ببرقع ... فإن لحت حاضت في الخدور العواتق
(Fear Allah and veil this beauty with a face-veil, for if you appear, maidens will menstruate in their chambers.)
This is in one of the transmissions of the verse reported by Abū al-Fatḥ ibn Jinnī. It is said that when a woman's desire grows intense, her menstrual blood flows. So the meaning of the verse: veil your beauty from them, or they will menstruate; though the transmission Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred is «ذابت» ("melted").
(حاشَ لِلَّهِ): that is, حاشا; the discussion of it will come in the section on Benefits.

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ نِسْوَةٌ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ): The wāw is a conjunction, so that the events of the story run in sequence. قال نسوة: a verb and an agent; وفي المدينة is an adjective (ṣifa) of نسوة. (امْرَأَتُ الْعَزِيزِ تُراوِدُ فَتاها عَنْ نَفْسِهِ قَدْ شَغَفَها حُبًّا): امرأة العزيز is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause تراود is the khabar; فتاها is a direct object; and عن نفسه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تراود; قد is a particle of certainty; and شغفها is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; حبا is a tamyīz converted from the agent. The clause قد شغفها is a ḥāl from the agent of تراود or from its object, and it is also permissible that it be a second khabar for امرأة. (إِنَّا لَنَراها فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ): inna and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause نراها is the khabar of inna; وفي ضلال is attached to نراها; and مبين is an adjective of ضلال. (فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَأً وَآتَتْ كُلَّ واحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ سِكِّيناً): The fāʾ is a conjunction, and لما is temporal or connective (rābiṭa); سمعت is a verb and a latent agent; بمكرهن is attached to سمعت; the clause أرسلت has no grammatical position; وإليهن is attached to أرسلت; وأعتدت is conjoined to أرسلت; ولهن is attached to أعتدت; متكأ is a direct object; وآتت is likewise a conjunction; كل واحدة is the first object of آتت; ومنهن is an adjective of واحدة; and سكينا is the second object of آتت. The word السكين is used as masculine and feminine; so said al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, and al-Jawharī said: "masculine is predominant in it."
(وَقالَتِ اخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ): The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause اخرج is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); وعليهن is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "appearing above them, towering over them with your captivating allure and your seizing beauty". (فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَهُ أَكْبَرْنَهُ وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ): The fāʾ is a conjunction, and لما is temporal or a connective particle; رأينه is a verb, an agent and a direct object; وقطعن is a verb and an agent; and أيديهن is a direct object. We do not hold the opinion of those who say that أكبرنه means "they menstruated" and that the hāʾ is for pause, for that is an artificial wittiness unbefitting the Qur'an. (وَقُلْنَ حاشَ لِلَّهِ ما هذا بَشَراً): وقلن is a verb and an agent; حاش is a noun of exoneration (tanzīh), in the position of accusative as an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); ولله is attached to an omitted ḥāl; more discussion of حاشا will come in the section on Benefits; ما is the Ḥijāzī negative, هذا is its noun and بشرا its predicate. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: "Al-Zamakhsharī said: and it was read ما هذا بشرى, i.e. 'something acquired by purchase', meaning 'this is something bought'; and you say هذا لك بشرى, i.e. 'a virgin'. And he said:
[Translator's note: the source text here is garbled or incomplete; the quotation of al-Zamakhsharī appears to break off and run into Abū Ḥayyān's words without a marker. It is translated as it stands.]
Giving ما the action of ليس is the ancient Ḥijāzī language, and in it the Qur'an came. End of quotation. He said "ancient" only because what is frequent in the Ḥijāzī language is the genitive predicate with the bāʾ, so you say ما زيد بقائم, and most of what occurs in the Qur'an is according to this; as for the accusative predicate, it belongs to the ancient Ḥijāzī language, so much so that the grammarians found no evidence for an accusative predicate in the poetry of the Ḥijāzīs apart from the poet's words: وأنا النذير بحرة مسودة ... يصل الجيوش إليكم قوادها
أبناؤها متكنفون أباهم ... حنقوا الصدور وما هم أولادها
(I am the warner of a blackened lava-field; its commanders will bring the armies to you. Its sons surround their father, their breasts full of rage, and they are not its children.)
Al-Farrāʾ, who was a hearer of the language, a reliable memoriser, said: The people of the Ḥijāz hardly speak except with the bāʾ. Since pronouncing with the bāʾ prevailed among the people of the Ḥijāz, al-Zamakhsharī said: "the ancient Ḥijāzī language", so the Qur'an came in both, the ancient and the other."
(إِنْ هذا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ): إن is negative, هذا a mubtadaʾ, إلا a particle of restriction, ملك the khabar and كريم an adjective. (قالَتْ فَذلِكُنَّ الَّذِي لُمْتُنَّنِي فِيهِ): فذلكن: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you wish to know him, then that is he"; and the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ. She did not say فهذا although he was present, and the flow of speech requires that, in order to raise his rank in beauty. And الذي is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. هو الذي ("he is the one who"); الذي was not made the khabar of the demonstrative, because the lām of distance attached to it required his remoteness from it, given the preceding exaltation of his rank in beauty and loveliness. وفيه is attached to لمتنني, i.e. "in his love" or "in soliciting him"; a verification of the omitted element will come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَلَقَدْ راوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ فَاسْتَعْصَمَ): The wāw is a conjunction, and the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of certainty; راودته is a verb, an agent and a direct object; وعن نفسه is attached to راودته; and فاستعصم: the fāʾ is a conjunction and استعصم is a past verb to which the sīn was added for intensity in refraining. (وَلَئِنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ ما آمُرُهُ لَيُسْجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُوناً مِنَ الصَّاغِرِينَ): The lām is the one that prepares for an oath (muwaṭṭiʾa), and إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; يفعل is an imperfect in the jussive and is the protasis; ما is a direct object, and the clause آمره is a ṣila, i.e. "that which I command him with". It is also valid for it to be maṣdarī, i.e. "my command"; the pronoun in آمره would return to the relative, i.e. "what I command with", so the preposition was dropped as it is dropped in أمرتك الخير; and the first object of آمر is omitted, the implied form being "ما آمره به". If you make ما maṣdarī it is permissible, and the pronoun returns to Yūsuf, i.e. "my command to him", meaning "the content of my command". The lām falls in the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, according to the rule when the two meet, indicated by the answer to the oath that is mentioned; the implied form is "ليسجنن وليكونن". In يسجنن there is the heavy nūn of emphasis, and in يكون the light nūn of emphasis; the noun of يكون is a latent pronoun, "he", and من الصاغرين is its khabar. (قالَ رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِي إِلَيْهِ): The clause is resumptive, with an explanatory resumption (istinʾāf bayānī), that is, one that is an answer to an implied question; for the women said to him, after they made him hear Zulaykhā's insistence: "Will you not obey your mistress?" He said, etc. رب is a vocative from which the vocative particle is omitted; السجن is a mubtadaʾ and أحب a khabar; and إلي is for clarification (li-l-tabyīn), the one that clarifies the agency of its genitive noun after whatever conveys love or hatred, of a verb of wonder or an elative; ومما is attached to أحب; the clause يدعونني is a ṣila, and it is an imperfect verb indeclinable on sukūn of the wāw; the first nūn is the nūn of the feminine plural and the second is the nūn of protection (wiqāya); so the wāw is not a pronoun but is the lām of the word, and it is not one of the five verbs that are raised by the presence of the nūn and put in the accusative and jussive by its dropping. He attributed the action to them because all of them called him to themselves; it is also said, because when they said to him "Will you not obey your mistress?", it was sound to attribute the calling to all of them. And إليه is attached to يدعونني.
(وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّي كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الْجاهِلِينَ): The wāw is a conjunction, إن is conditional and لا is negative; تصرف is the protasis and the agent is latent, "you"; وعني is attached to تصرف and كيدهن is a direct object; أصب is the apodosis and the agent is latent, "I"; وإليهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أصب; وأكن is conjoined to أصب and the noun of أكن is latent, "I"; and من الجاهلين is the khabar of أكن.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying, the Exalted: «ما هذا بشرا إن هذا إلا ملك كريم»
There are two intertwined arts. The first is apparent: the intensive simile (tashbīh baligh), for they likened Yūsuf to an angel without mentioning the particle of comparison.
