(السِّقايَةَ): a drinking vessel from which water is given to drink. It is the ṣuwāʿ mentioned later; the king used to drink from it, so it was called siqāya with regard to its first state and ṣāʿ with regard to its later one, because the ṣāʿ is a measure of volume. It was said it was an elongated vessel resembling the makkūk; it was said it was the Persian makkūk whose two ends meet, from which the non-Arabs drink; it was said it was of silver gilded with gold; it was said it was of gold; it was said it was studded with jewels.
(رَحْلِ): al-raḥl, with a fatḥa on the rāʾ, is what is placed on the camel's back, like a saddle; what is meant here is the place where he rides.
(الْعِيرُ): with a kasra on the ʿayn, camels on which loads are carried because they go to and fro (taʿīr); it was said: a caravan of donkeys, and then it became common so that every caravan was called ʿīr as if it were the plural of ʿayr. What is meant is the people of the caravan, as will come under Rhetoric.
(صُواعَ): al-ṣuwāʿ with a ḍamma on the ṣād, and al-ṣāʿ, are two dialectal forms with one meaning; it is the measure of volume. It has already been mentioned that it is the siqāya, and this vessel was taken as a measure only because of the scarcity of what is measured with at that time.
(السَّارِقُ): the one who steals goods from safe places. The Arabs have a detailed classification of thieves. If he waylays caravans, he is a liṣṣ and a farḍūb. If he steals camels, he is a khārib; or sheep, he is an aḥmaṣ, and al-ḥamīṣa is a stolen sheep. If he steals dirhams from between a person's fingers, he is a qaffāf. If he slits pockets to get at them, he is a ṭarrār. If he specialises in theft, wickedness and depravity, he is a ṭamil. If he steals, commits adultery and harms people, he is a dāʿir. If he is wicked and loathsome, he is an ʿifr, and "ʿifrīya nifrīya". If he is the worst of thieves, he is an ʿamrūṭ. If he guides thieves and insinuates himself among them, he is a shaṣṣ. If he eats and drinks with them and guards their goods but does not steal with them, he is a lafīf.
As for al-liṣṣ, the lām may take three vowels, and some lexicographers distinguished between them, saying:
إغلاق باب ستر فعل لصّ ... وسارق بالحركات لصّ
جمع الألصّ من رجال لصّ ... منضم أضراس فكن ذا خبر
(Closing a door, a covering, the act of a thief; and a thief with the vowelings, liṣṣ. The plural of al-alaṣṣ among men is luṣṣ, one whose teeth are joined; so be well informed.)
[Translator's note: the two verses are rendered as given in the source, whose wording appears corrupt; the gloss is tentative.]

* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُمْ): لما is temporal or connective. من: a preposition. حيث: an adverb indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive through من; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to دخلوا, and the meaning is "separately". The clause أمرهم أبوهم is annexed to the adverb.
(ما كانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): the clause is the answer to لما; it was also said that the answer is آوى إليه أخاه. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: it is the answer to the first لما and the second. ما is negative. كان is a defective past verb, and its subject is the pronoun of separation indicated by the preceding speech. عنهم: attached to يغني. من الله: a ḥāl. من: a redundant preposition. شيء: genitive in form, accusative in position as a direct object.
(إِلَّا حاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضاها): a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) in the sense of "but a need in the soul of Yaʿqūb which he fulfilled", namely his solicitude for them. في نفس: an adjective. يعقوب: a muḍāf ilayhi. The clause قضاها is an adjective of حاجة.
(وَإِنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِما عَلَّمْناهُ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the واو is circumstantial. إن and its subject; the shifted lām; ذو علم is the khabar of إن. The clause علمناه is a ṣila. ولكن: the واو is also circumstantial; لكن and its subject; the clause لا يعلمون is the khabar.
(وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلى يُوسُفَ آوى إِلَيْهِ أَخاهُ): its parsing has preceded. أخاه: the object of آوى, and the clause is the answer to the first لما and the second.
(قالَ إِنِّي أَنَا أَخُوكَ فَلا تَبْتَئِسْ بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): إن and its subject; أنا is a mubtadaʾ, أخوك a khabar, and the clause is the khabar of إن. The clause is resumptive, and so is every case where a reply was required and its reply was mentioned and then قال came after it: it is resumptive. The فاء is the eloquent fāʾ. لا is prohibitive. تبتئس: an imperfect verb jussive through لا. بما: attached to تبتئس. The clause كانوا is a ṣila, and the clause يعملون is the khabar of كانوا.
(فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهازِهِمْ جَعَلَ السِّقايَةَ فِي رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ): the فاء is a conjunction indicating their eager desire to travel. لما is temporal or connective. جهزهم: a verb, an agent and a direct object. بجهازهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جهزهم. The clause جعل السقاية في رحل أخيه has no grammatical position. في رحل: attached to جعل.
(ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا الْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسارِقُونَ): ثم is a conjunction implying delay. أذن مؤذن: a verb and an agent, that is, a caller called. It was conjoined with ثم to indicate Yūsuf's giving them respite until they set off. أيتها: the one addressed, with the vocative particle omitted; it is an indefinite specific noun (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is for alerting. العير: a badal from أيتها. إن and its subject; the shifted lām; سارقون is its khabar.
(قالُوا وَأَقْبَلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ ماذا تَفْقِدُونَ): the واو is circumstantial, with an implied قد. عليهم: attached to أقبلوا. ماذا: an interrogative noun, a fronted object of تفقدون; or ما is an interrogative noun and ذا a relative noun, the khabar, and the clause تفقدون is the ṣila. What was said about ماذا has already preceded.
(قالُوا نَفْقِدُ صُواعَ الْمَلِكِ): the clause نفقد صواع الملك is the quoted speech.
(وَلِمَنْ جاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ): the واو is a conjunction. ولمن: a fronted khabar. The clause جاء به is a ṣila. حمل بعير: a postponed mubtadaʾ. The واو is a conjunction. أنا: a mubtadaʾ. به: attached to زعيم. زعيم, that is, a guarantor: the khabar.
(قالُوا تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ ما جِئْنا لِنُفْسِدَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما كُنَّا سارِقِينَ): the tāʾ is a particle of genitive and oath. لله: the word of majesty, genitive through the oath-tāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "we swear". The lām occurs in the answer to the oath, or is an emphasis of the first oath. قد: a particle of affirmation. علمتم: a verb and an agent. ما: negative. جئنا: a verb and an agent. لنفسد: the lām is for causation, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "we". في الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نفسد. وما كنا: ما is negative; kāna and its subject; سارقين is its khabar. They swore with the tāʾ, among the particles of oath, because of the sense of wonder it usually carries, as if they wondered at being accused of this matter. The tāʾ enters an oath only on the word Allah among His names, the Exalted; you do not say تالرحمن or تالرحيم, but its entering on al-Rabb, on al-Raḥmān, and on "your life" has been reported from the Arabs; they said ترب الكعبة, تالرحمن and تحياتك.

* Rhetoric:
In the words of the Exalted "أيتها العير انكم لسارقون" there is a mixed figurative expression (majāz mursal) whose relation is contiguity, the meaning being the people of the caravan, as in the hadith "يا خيل الله اركبي" (O horses of Allah, mount!). Concerning al-ʿīr, a question arose in the assembly of Sayf al-Dawla ibn Ḥamdān, the questioner being Ibn Khālawayh and the one questioned being al-Mutanabbī. Ibn Khālawayh said: "al-baʿīr is also the donkey, and this is a rare usage which I put to al-Mutanabbī in the presence of Sayf al-Dawla; he had in him some haughtiness and arrogance, and became flustered. I said: what is meant by al-baʿīr in the words of the Exalted «ولمن جاء به حمل بعير» is the donkey, because Yaʿqūb and his son Yūsuf, peace be upon them, were in the land of Canaan, where there were no camels; they used to get provisions on donkeys." Muqātil ibn Sulaymān mentioned it likewise in his commentary.

dervis-irab:21-24.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَثْواهُ): his place of abode. One says ثوى بالمكان and أثوى, "he stayed"; and one says فلان أكرم مثواي ("so-and-so honoured my abode"), طال بي الثواء ("my stay has been long"), وهو أبو مثواي and وهي أم مثواي for the one with whom you are lodging. He said:
أفي كل يوم أم مثوى تسوسني ... تنفّض أثوابي وتسألني ما اسسي
(Is it every day that the mother of my lodging manages me, shaking out my clothes and asking me what my lineage is?) «[Translator's note: the last word of the verse is as printed in the source and appears corrupted.]»
(أَشُدَّهُ): There are three views about al-ashudd. The first is the view of Sībawayh: that it is a plural whose singular is shidda, like niʿma and anʿum. The second is the view of al-Kisāʾī: that its singular is shadd on the pattern of qufl. The third is that it is a plural with no singular from its own wording, and this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda; it is from al-shadd, which is tying upon a thing and knotting it. Al-Rāghib said: in it is an alert that when a person reaches this measure, his constitution on which he is becomes strong and hardly leaves him. It is said that al-ashudd is eighteen years, and twenty, and thirty-three, and forty-three; and it is said that its furthest limit is sixty-two.
(راوَدَتْهُ): al-murāwada is a mufāʿala form from rāda yarūdu, when one comes and goes, as though the meaning were "she beguiled him away from himself", that is, she did what a beguiler does to his companion regarding something he does not want to let go of his hand, scheming to overcome him over it and take it from him. It is an expression for contriving to have intercourse with him. From it comes al-rāʾid, the seeker of water and pasture. It is a mufāʿala from one party, like a creditor's demanding, a debtor's procrastinating, a physician's treating, and their like, in which the act is from one side and its cause from the other; for these acts, even though they proceed from both sides, since their causes proceed from the other side, are made as though they proceeded from both. This is a subtle path, built on a delicate consideration, the verification of which is that the cause of a thing stands in its place and is called by its name, as in their saying «كما تدين تدان», that is, "as you requite, you will be requited", for the act of the initiator, though not a requital, being a cause of requital, is called by its name. Likewise the intention to rise for prayer and the intention to recite the Qur'an, since they are a cause of rising and reciting, are expressed by them, so it is said إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة and فإذا قرأت القرآن; and this is a regular, continuous rule. It is also possible that the mufāʿala form is meant for mere intensification. It is also said that the form is on its usual pattern, in the sense that she asked him for the act and he asked her to desist. It is also possible that it is from al-ruwayd, which is gentleness and graciousness, and its transitivity with عن is because it includes the meaning of beguiling, so the meaning is "she beguiled him away from himself", that is, she did what a beguiler does to his companion regarding something he does not want to let go of his hand, while he schemes to take it from him.
(هَيْتَ لَكَ): It is a noun of a verb, containing the pronoun of the one addressed, like صه and مه, and what it names is "hurry". One says هيت when calling someone. The poet said:
أبلغ أمير المؤمنين أخا ... العراق إذا أتيتا
أن العراق وأهله ... سلم عليك فهيت هيتا
(Convey to the Commander of the Faithful, brother of Iraq, when you come: Iraq and its people are at peace with you, so hurry, hurry.) He means the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. It is intransitive, not taking an object, just as what it names is so. It has three dialects: hayta with fatḥa, hayta with ḍamma, and hayta with kasra. And «لك» in your saying هيت لك is an explanation for the one addressed, brought after the sentence no longer needed it, as it is in سقيا لك; do you not see that سقيا does not need لك, because its meaning is "may Allah give you drink"? It was brought only for emphasis and addition, and it is the same in هيت لك. It is also said that هيت is a noun of a past verb meaning "I have made myself ready" (tahayyaʾtu). In al-Qāmūs: وهيت لك with three vowels on the last letter, and sometimes with kasra on the first letter, meaning "come". The scholar al-Ghunaymī said: it is possible that the latent pronoun in تهيأت is "هي" (she), and it was read تهيأت with sukūn on the tāʾ; this is a report of her speech, as you say قال زيد والله ليفعلن, meaning "he said: by Allah, I shall do".
(مَعاذَ اللَّهِ): This is one of the maṣdars of عاذ يعوذ: عوذا, معاذا, عوذة, عياذة and عياذا. The meaning of أعوذ بالله is "I take hold of, and refrain by Allah's help, from the accursed Satan". It is recited from the rajaz poet Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, or ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib:
أنفي لك اللهم عان راغم ... مهما تجشّمني فإني جاشم
عذت بما عاذ به ابراهم
(My nose, O Allah, is a submissive captive to You; whatever You burden me with, I shall bear it. I have sought refuge in that in which Ibrāhām sought refuge.) He means by it Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. Among the Arabs are those who say "Ibrāhām", and so Ibn ʿĀmir read, because Ibrāhīm is a foreign name, and when the Arabs Arabize it they vary its forms; some of them say "Ibrahm" without an alif. The poet said:
نحن آل الله في كعبته ... لم يزل ذاك على عهد إبرهم
(We are the family of Allah in His Kaʿba; that has not ceased since the time of Ibrahm.) From al-Farrāʾ, he said: "The Arabs say نعوذ بالله من طئة الذليل, that is, 'I seek refuge in Allah from being trodden on by a lowly person'." And in Lisān al-ʿArab: "the treading of the lowly is from his seeking refuge in Allah."

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الَّذِي اشْتَراهُ مِنْ مِصْرَ لِامْرَأَتِهِ أَكْرِمِي مَثْواهُ) It is conjoined to an omitted clause, that is, "they entered Egypt and put him up for sale, and the ʿAzīz (chief minister) of Egypt, who was over the treasuries of Egypt, bought him, and his name was Quṭfīr." قال is a past verb; الذي is the fāʿil, and the clause اشتراه is a ṣila; من مصر is a ḥāl; لامرأته is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قال; the clause أكرمي مثواه is the content of the saying, and it is a verb, agent and object, and its explanation has already been given. (عَسى أَنْ يَنْفَعَنا أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُ وَلَداً) عسى is one of the verbs of hope, and its noun is latent; أن and what is in its scope is its khabar, and what is said about it has already been given; أو is a conjunction; نتخذه is an imperfect verb conjoined to ينفعنا, the ـه is a first direct object and ولدا a second direct object. (وَكَذلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ) وكذلك is an adjective of a maṣdar, that is, "like that establishing"; مكنا is a past verb and agent, and ليوسف is attached to it, for the verb مكّن is transitive by itself and with the lām as here; and في الأرض is a ḥāl. (وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُ مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحادِيثِ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is causal; نعلمه is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the ـه is a mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted word, that is, "and in order that We teach him, We established him"; something like this has already occurred in «ولتكملوا العدة». من تأويل الأحاديث is attached to نعلمه. Al-Jalāl gave it i'rab on the basis of the wāw being redundant, so that it is attached to the mentioned مكنا. (وَاللَّهُ غالِبٌ عَلى أَمْرِهِ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) والله is a mubtadaʾ and غالب the khabar; على أمره is attached to غالب; the wāw is circumstantial; lākinna and its noun; and the clause لا يعلمون is its khabar. (وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ آتَيْناهُ حُكْماً وَعِلْماً وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ) لما is temporal or connective; بلغ أشده is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; آتيناه is verb, agent and direct object; حكما is a second direct object and علما is conjoined to it; كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; and نجزي المحسنين is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object. (وَراوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِها عَنْ نَفْسِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; راودته is a verb with a fronted direct object; التي is the fāʿil; هو is a mubtadaʾ and في بيتها its khabar, and the nominal clause is a ṣila; and عن نفسه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to راودته. (وَغَلَّقَتِ الْأَبْوابَ وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ) These are conjoined clauses; the i'rab of هيت لك was given in the section on Vocabulary. The name of the woman who solicited him was Zulaykhāʾ, with fatḥa on the zāy and kasra on the lām. He did not say "and Zulaykhā solicited him" or "the wife of the ʿAzīz", either because it is distasteful to state the name in connection with soliciting and scheming to seek intercourse, or to conceal her from others lest they accuse her, or to further confirm the attribution of the predicate to its subject, for his being in her house and her being able to look upon his beauty from time to time is what establishes her soliciting; or to further confirm the intended point, because his refusal of her despite her complete power over him indicates his purity and the cleanness of his hem. It is also said that He chose it in the verse because sharing in the knowledge of her name is possible, and the genus may be meant in "wife of the ʿAzīz", unlike the relative noun. (قالَ مَعاذَ اللَّهِ إِنَّهُ رَبِّي أَحْسَنَ مَثْوايَ) معاذ الله is accusative as a maṣdar, that is, "I seek refuge in Allah with refuge"; and إنه ربي: inna, its noun and its khabar. The pronoun may refer to Quṭfīr who bought him, and its meaning is "my master and my owner", meaning Quṭfīr, and the clause أحسن مثواي is a ḥāl. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to the situation (shaʾn) and the matter; and ربي is a mubtadaʾ, the clause أحسن مثواي its khabar, and the clause the khabar of إنّ. It is also possible that the hāʾ is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted. Some of them have regarded the first as unlikely, and said it is very unlikely that a noble prophet would call a created being his lord, even in the sense of master, because he was not in reality owned. (إِنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ) inna and its noun; the clause لا يفلح الظالمون is its khabar; and the pronoun refers here to the shaʾn.
(وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِها لَوْلا أَنْ رَأى بُرْهانَ رَبِّهِ) The lām is the response to the omitted oath; قد is a particle of confirmation; همت is a past verb and هي its fāʿil; به is attached to همت; وهمّ is a past verb and هو its fāʿil; بها is attached to هم; لولا is a particle indicating prevention because of existence; أن and what is in its scope is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, "had it not been for his seeing the proof of his Lord present before him"; and the response to لولا is omitted, that is, "he would have committed it with her". There is disagreement about the proof (burhān) that he saw, and the exegetes have long discussion on it, to be consulted in the large works; it is enough for us to quote the words of Abū Ḥayyān. He said: "What I choose is that Yūsuf, peace be upon him, never at all inclined toward her; rather, it is negated because of the sight of the proof, as you say: 'You would have sinned had Allah not protected you.' And I do not say that the response to لولا precedes it, although no evidence stands against that being impossible; indeed, the explicit conditional particles that govern are disputed as to whether their responses may precede them, and the Kufans held that, and among the leading Basrans Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī and Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Mubarrad; rather we say that the response to لولا is omitted because what precedes it indicates it, as the majority of Basrans say about the Arabs' saying أنت ظالم إن فعلت, which they take to mean إن فعلت فأنت ظالم; and his saying أنت ظالم does not indicate the establishment of wrongdoing; rather it is established on the assumption that the act exists. Likewise here the implied meaning is: had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have inclined toward her, so the inclination would have existed on the assumption of the absence of seeing the proof; but the seeing of the proof existed, so the inclination was negated." This is excellent speech that supports what we held in the i'rab, so ponder it.
There is no disagreement that Yūsuf, peace be upon him, did not commit the indecency; the disagreement is only about the occurrence of inclination from him. Some exegetes held that he inclined and intended the indecency and did some of its preliminaries; and the author of al-Kashshāf was excessive in his censure of these, so refer to him. Others absolved him of inclination as well, and that is the correct view, as preceded in the words of Abū Ḥayyān. Imam al-Rāzī in his Tafsīr al-Kabīr has a point that is worth citing. He said: "Those who have a connection with this incident are Yūsuf, peace be upon him, the woman, her husband, the women, the witnesses, the Lord of the worlds, and Iblīs, and all of them spoke of the innocence of Yūsuf, peace be upon him, from sin, so no Muslim has any room to hesitate in this matter. As for Yūsuf, for his saying: «هي راودتني عن نفسي», and his saying «رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه». As for the woman, for her saying «ولقد راودته عن نفسه». As for her husband, for his saying: «إنه من كيدكن إن كيدكن عظيم». As for the women, for their saying: «امرأة العزيز تراود فتاها عن نفسه قد شغفها حبا إنا لنراها في ضلال مبين», and their saying «حاشا لله ما علمنا عليه من سوء». As for the witnesses, for His saying, the Exalted: «وشهد شاهد من أهلها» to the end. As for the testimony of Allah the Exalted, His saying, mighty is the Speaker: «كذلك لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء إنه من عبادنا المخلصين». As for Iblīs's acknowledgement of that, it is his saying «فبعزتك لأغوينهم أجمعين إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين»; so Iblīs acknowledged that it is not possible to misguide the sincere servants, and Allah the Exalted said that he is of «عبادنا المخلصين», so Iblīs acknowledged that he did not misguide him. At this point we say: these ignorant people who attributed scandal to Yūsuf, peace be upon him, if they are among the followers of the religion of Allah, let them accept Allah's testimony to his purity; and if they are among the followers of Iblīs and his troops, let them accept Iblīs's acknowledgement of his purity."
(كَذلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ السُّوءَ وَالْفَحْشاءَ) كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "We confirmed him with a confirmation like that"; the lām is attached to that omitted word. It is also sound for it to be in the position of the nominative, the implied meaning being "the matter is like that", but the accusative is better; similar cases have already preceded. السوء is a mafʿūl bihi and الفحشاء is conjoined to السوء.
(إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبادِنَا الْمُخْلَصِينَ) inna and its noun; من عبادنا is the khabar; and المخلصين is an adjective of عبادنا.

* Rhetoric:
Among the considerations favouring the subject-noun (al-musnad ilayhi) being a relative noun is the confirmation of the purpose for which the speech is driven, and that is in His saying, the Exalted: «وراودته التي هو في بيتها عن نفسه». For the purpose for which the speech is driven is the innocence of Yūsuf, peace be upon him; had it been said "the wife of the ʿAzīz solicited him" or "Zulaykhā", it would not have conveyed what the relative noun conveys by virtue of its ṣila, so it is more indicative of the purpose for which it is driven, namely purity. For if he was in her house and was able to attain what was wanted from her, that is, what she wanted and not what he wanted, and nevertheless he abstained from her and did not do it, that was the utmost in purity from indecency; so there was in the relative noun an additional confirmation of the purpose, which is purity.
Another view:
It is said that its meaning is a further confirmation of the predicate, that is, the soliciting, because of the excessive mixing and familiarity in it; had He said Zulaykhā or the wife of the ʿAzīz, it would not have conveyed what the relative noun conveys, of the mention of the cause that is its concomitant, in confirming the soliciting by virtue of his being in her house.

Another view:
It is said: it is a confirmation of the subject, because of the possibility of vagueness and sharing of names in "the wife of the ʿAzīz" or "Zulaykhā" had He mentioned either of them; and that does not arise in «التي هو في بيتها», because she is one specific, particular woman.

dervis-irab:102-107.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَرَصْتَ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: ḥaraṣa ʿalayhi ḥarṣan (of the pattern ḍaraba) when he strove; the noun is al-ḥirṣ with kasra. Ḥaraṣa ʿalā al-dunyā (of the pattern ḍaraba) and ḥariṣa ḥarṣan (of the pattern taʿiba) is a dialectal form when he desired it with a blameworthy desire. The scholars of the language said: ḥaraṣa ʿalā al-shayʾ and he is ḥarīṣ, among a people who are ḥirāṣ; "How eager you are for the world!"; greed is ill-omened; "May Allah not guard the greedy". Ḥaraṣa al-qaṣṣār (the fuller) the garment means he tore it; "your garment has a ḥarṣa", and "a ḥāriṣa struck him", which is one of the wounds that split the skin; "ḥamā muḥarraṣ: mukaddaḥ" [Translator's note: this phrase is printed so in the source and its sense is unclear]; and "al-ḥāriṣa and al-ḥarīṣa poured down", which is the cloud heavy in rainfall, and "the face of the earth was scraped". Al-Ḥuwayda said:
ظلم البطاح بها انهلال حريصة ... فصفا النّطاف بها بعيد المقلع
(The wronged wide valleys, with the pouring of a scraping downpour, so the pools in them became clear after the cloud cleared.) [Translator's note: the verse is translated as printed; its wording is obscure.] And "I saw the Arabs eager for the falling of the ḥarīṣa."
(غاشِيَةٌ): a punishment that overwhelms them. It was also said: whatever of torment engulfs them and covers them. In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: al-ghāshiya is the feminine of al-ghāshī, and the covering (the plural being ghawāshin), and the calamity, and the Resurrection, and a disease in the belly; and "ghāshiyat fulān" are his servants and visitors.

* I'rab:
(ذلِكَ مِنْ أَنْباءِ الْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ) ذلك is a demonstrative in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and من أنباء الغيب is its khabar; the clause نوحيه إليك is a ḥāl, and it may be in the position of nominative as a second khabar. In this noble verse is a proof that admits no doubt of the prophethood of Muḥammad ﷺ, because he was unlettered, did not read books, did not meet scholars, and did not travel to any place other than the town where he grew up, and despite that he brought this long story, gathering the conditions and characteristics of the story form that modern ages invented. (وَما كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ أَجْمَعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَمْكُرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; كنت: كان and its ism; ولديهم is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar of كنت; إذ is an adverb attached to what the first adverb is attached to, namely the omitted "being present"; the clause أجمعوا is annexed to the adverb; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāl); هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يمكرون a khabar; and the clause is a ḥāl. (وَما أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is a negative in the Hijazi manner, hence the redundant bāʾ in its khabar; أكثر الناس is its ism; the wāw is parenthetical; لو is conditional; حرصت is a verb and agent, and the clause is parenthetical between the Hijazi ما and its khabar. A detailed discussion of the parenthetical clause will come in the section of Benefits. The bāʾ is a redundant preposition and مؤمنين is genitive by the bāʾ in form, in the position of accusative as the khabar of ما; and the answer to لو is omitted, i.e., "they would not have believed".
(وَما تَسْئَلُهُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; تسألهم is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, and the hāʾ a direct object; وعليه is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of أجر, and the pronoun refers to the Qur'an; من is a redundant particle and أجر is genitive by من in form, accusative in position as a direct object; إن is negative; هو is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; ذكر is the khabar of هو; and للعالمين is an adjective of ذكر. (وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ آيَةٍ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) The discussion of كأين and the two khabarī كم has already been given at length. It is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; ومن آية is a tamyīz (specification) governed by من; and في السموات والأرض is an adjective of آية. (يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْها وَهُمْ عَنْها مُعْرِضُونَ) The clause يمرون is a khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is كأين; وعليها is attached to يمرون; وهم: the wāw is circumstantial and هم is a mubtadaʾ; وعنها is attached to معرضون; and معرضون is their khabar; the nominal clause is a ḥāl. It is permissible that في السموات والأرض be a khabar of كأين, with the clause يمرون an adjective of آية. (وَما يُؤْمِنُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ بِاللَّهِ إِلَّا وَهُمْ مُشْرِكُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; يؤمن أكثرهم is an imperfect verb and agent; وبالله is attached to يؤمن; إلا is a particle of restriction; the wāw is circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ and مشركون a khabar; and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (أَفَأَمِنُوا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ غاشِيَةٌ مِنْ عَذابِ اللَّهِ) The hamza is for reproachful interrogation, containing the sense of rebuke and threat; the fāʾ is a conjunction; أمنوا is a verb and agent; and the interpreted maṣdar of أن تأتيهم is the direct object of أمنوا; the hāʾ is the object of تأتي; غاشية is the agent of تأتي; and من عذاب الله is an adjective of غاشية. (أَوْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ) أو تأتيهم is conjoined to the preceding تأتيهم; الساعة is the agent of تأتيهم; بغتة is a ḥāl; the wāw is circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يشعرون a khabar; and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «وما كنت لديهم» is an art called in the science of bayān al-iḥtijāj al-naẓarī (argument by reasoning), and some call it al-madhhab al-kalāmī (the theologians' method), which is that one binds the adversary to what is necessarily entailed by this argument. Its discussion has already been given. In it there is a bitter mockery of them, because everyone knew that Muḥammad ﷺ was not with them; so when he reports it and narrates this wondrous narrative, no doubt arises that it is not from him.
2- In His saying «وما أكثر الناس، ولو حرصت، بمؤمنين» is the art of parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ). Its mention and definition have already been given, and we add here something that relates to an interesting rhetorical discussion, namely that parenthesis is of two kinds. One does not occur in speech except for a benefit, and it runs the course of emphasis; the other occurs in speech without benefit, and then either its entry is like its absence, or it affects the composition with defect and the meaning with corruption. The first kind is like this verse. The benefit of the parenthesis is in two respects. The first is depicting the Prophet's ﷺ eagerness for the faith of his people and their guidance, his consuming himself to turn them from their error and divert them from the places of mistake and the places of misguidance, and his exposing himself to harm in the cause of this eagerness, though knowing it is futile and that it is impossible for them to desist from what they are in. The second respect is depicting their obstinacy, the denial of their mentality, their insistence on the error they have embarked on and are holding to, and their stubbornness and arrogance in what the established, luminous proofs and evidences cannot help with. The noble Qur'an is full of this kind and it will come to you in its places, Allah willing. We have cited a group of fine poetry whose parenthesis added to it delicacy and sweetness; and how beautiful is the saying of Ibn al-Muʿadhdhab al-Saʿdī:
فلو سألت سراة الحي سلمى ... على أن قد تلوّن بي زماني
لخبرها ذو وأحساب قومي ... وأعدائي فكلّ قد بلاني
(Had Salmā asked the chiefs of the tribe — though my time has changed colours with me — the men of rank of my people and my enemies would have told her, for each has tried me.) [Translator's note: the second verse is printed in the source as «لخبرها ذو وأحساب قومي», and the sentence below reads «ذو وأحساب»; translated as printed.] This is a parenthesis between لو and its answer, and it is among the finest and rarest parentheses. Its implied form is "Had Salmā asked the chiefs of the tribe, the men of rank of my people and my enemies would have told her." The benefit of his saying «على أن قد تلوّن بي زماني» is that they report about me despite the changing colours of time with me, meaning the shifting of its states from good to evil; and he is not like one whom time has tested and whose substance it has made clear, like others whom it has not tested and whose substance it has not made clear.
As for the second kind, which occurs in speech without benefit, it is of two sorts:
The first: its entry into the speech is like its absence; it gains neither beauty nor ugliness by it. Among that is al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī's saying, lamenting al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir:
يقول رجال يجهلون خليقتي ... لعل زيادا- لا أبا لك- غافل
(Men who do not know my nature say: "Perhaps Ziyād — may you have no father — is heedless.") His saying "lā abā laka" is a parenthesis with no benefit except to complete the metre, and it affects it with neither beauty nor ugliness. Similar is the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abī Salmā:
سئمت تكاليف الحياة ومن يعش ... ثمانين حولا، لا أبا لك، يسأم
(I am weary of life's burdens, and whoever lives eighty years — may you have no father — grows weary.)
The second: that which affects the speech with defect and the meaning with corruption. We shall cite examples of it so that the intelligent may avoid them. Among that is the saying of one of them:
فقد، والشك: بيّن لي، عناء ... بوشك فراقهم صرد يصيح
([Roughly:] A crying shrike has made plain to me, doubt aside, the distress of their imminent parting.) He put forward «بوشك فراقهم», which is dependent on «يصيح», and يصيح is an adjective of صرد, and that is ugly. Do you not see that it is not permitted to say "this, from such a place, a man arrived today"? A dependent may occur only where its governor may occur; so just as it is not permitted to put the adjective before its described noun, it is likewise not permitted to put what is attached to it before its described noun. Furthermore, among the bad parentheses in it is the separation between «قد» and the verb, which is «بيّن», and that is very ugly, owing to the strength of the connection between قد and the verbs it enters, so much so that they count it as a part of the verb; for that reason the oath-lām meant to emphasise the verb is introduced upon it, as in His saying «ولقد علموا لمن اشتراه». Further, the verse has a third fault, which is the separation between the mubtadaʾ, which is الشك, and the khabar, which is عناء, by «بيّن لي»; and a fourth fault, which is the separation between the verb «بيّن» and its agent «صرد» by the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is «عناء». So the meaning of the verse, as you see, is like a disfigured image whose members have been moved, some to the place of others.
From this sort is the saying of another:
نظرت وشخصي مطلع الشمس ظله ... إلى الغرب حتى ظله الشمس قد عقل
(I looked, my figure at the sun's rising, its shadow toward the west, until its shadow had held back the sun.) He meant: "I looked at the rising-place of the sun, my figure's shadow toward the setting, until it checked the sun", i.e., stood level with it. On this reading he has separated, by «مطلع الشمس», the mubtadaʾ, which is «شخصي», from its khabar, the clause «ظله إلى الغرب»; and coarser and more repellent than that, he separated the verb from its agent by an "alien" (ajnabī). This is something silence is better than.
And since we have spoken about parenthesis from the technical rhetorical side, we cannot avoid treating it from the grammatical side, for the grammarians have established that it occurs in places:
1- Between the verb and its nominative, as in the saying of one of them:
شجاك أظن ربع الظاعنينا ... ولم تعبأ بعذل العاذلينا
(The abode of the departing ones, I think, has grieved you, and you paid no heed to the blame of the blamers.) شجاك is a past verb and its agent is ربع الظاعنينا, and the clause أظن separates them. This parenthetical clause gives strengthening, because when it is said "the abode of the departing ones grieved you", it may be that this is thought or imagined, so he reported that it is thought. In this verse it is also possible that ربع be accusative as the first object of أظن, with the clause شجاك as its second object, its implied form being "I think the abode of the departing ones has grieved you".
2- Between the verb and its accusative object, as in the poet's saying:
وبدلت، والدهر ذو تبدل، ... هيفا دبورا بالصبا والشمأل
(And, time being given to change, a hot south wind in place of the east wind and the north wind has been substituted.) بدلت is a passive past verb and the deputy agent refers to the wind; والدهر ذو تبدل is parenthetical; هيفا is the object of بدلت, i.e., a ḥayfāʾ wind, meaning hot; and the bāʾ in بالصبا enters upon what is left, as is the rule for the bāʾ that follows بدل. Al-ṣabā is the wind that blows from the east at the equality of night and day, and al-shamʾal is the wind that comes from the direction of the pole.
3- Between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar, as in his saying:
وفيهن، والأيام يعثرن بالفتى ... نوادب لا يمللنه ونوائح
(And among them — while the days trip up the young man — are mourners who do not tire of him, and wailing women.) He separated فيهن, which is a fronted khabar, from نوادب, which is a postponed mubtadaʾ, by the clause والأيام يعثرن بالفتى.
4- Between what was originally a mubtadaʾ and a khabar, as in the saying of ʿAwf ibn Muḥallim:
إن الثمانين وبلغتها ... قد أحوجت سمعي إلى ترجمان
(Eighty — may you reach it — has made my hearing need an interpreter.) His saying «وبلغتها» is an invocatory clause interposed between the ism of إن and its khabar, which were originally a mubtadaʾ and a khabar.
5- Between the condition and its apodosis, as in the saying of the Exalted «فإن لم تفعلوا. ولن تفعلوا، فاتقوا النار»; its i'rab has already been given.
6- Between the oath and its answer, as in the saying of al-Nābigha:
لعمري وما عمري عليّ بهين ... لقد نطقت بطلا عليّ الأقارع
(By my life — and my life is not light to me — the Aqāriʿ have spoken falsehood against me.) He interposed the clause «وما عمري علي بهين» between the oath and its answer.
7- Between the described noun and its adjective, as in the saying of the Exalted «وانه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم»; the clause «لو تعلمون» is interposed between the described noun, which is «قسم», and its adjective, which is «عظيم».
8- Between the relative noun and its ṣila, as in the poet's saying:
واني لرام نظرة قبل التي ... لعلي وإن شطت نواها أزورها
(I shall cast a glance before the one — perhaps, though her destination be distant, I shall visit her.) He interposed «لعلي» between التي and its ṣila, which is «أزورها»; the khabar of لعل is omitted, i.e., "perhaps I shall do that".
9- Between the particle of futurity and the verb, as in Zuhayr's saying:
وما أدري وسوف أخال أدري ... أقوم آل حصن أم نساء
(I do not know — and I shall, I fancy, come to know — whether the family of Ḥiṣn are men or women.) This parenthesis is within another parenthesis, for سوف and what follows it is a parenthesis between أدري and the interrogative clause.
10- Between the particle of negation and what it negates, as in his saying:
فلا وأبي دهماء زالت عزيزة ... على قومها ما دام للزند قادح
(No, by the father of Dahmāʾ, she has not ceased to be honoured among her people as long as the fire-stick has a striker.)
There are other places which we have passed over because of the rarity of their occurrence; they may be consulted in the longer works.

dervis-irab:42-49.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِضْعَ سِنِينَ): البضع is what lies between three and nine, and most reports say he stayed in it seven years. One of the scholars of the language said: البضع, with kasra and with fatḥa, is what lies between one and five according to Abū ʿUbayda, while others said between one and ten. And البضع with fatḥa is "a slit", and البضع with damma is "intercourse". Some of them said:
شقّ وري وجماع بضع ... ما بين واحد وعشر بضع
(Slitting, watering and intercourse are بضع; and between one and ten is بضع.)
In al-Asās: "I have بضعة عشر men and بضع عشرة women" (the masculine with the tāʾ and the feminine without it, following the rule of numbers). "And I stayed with him بضع سنين, which is between three and ten." In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: "البضع and البضع is a portion of the night, and what lies between three and nine. One says بضع سنين and بضع عشرة of women and بضع وعشرون woman, and with the masculine بضعة عشر of men and بضعة وعشرون man. It is obligatory to put بضع first, so one does not say عشرون وبضع." Al-Ḥarīrī said in Durrat al-Ghawwāṣ: "بضع is most used for what lies between three and ten, and he traced that back to the Prophet ﷺ in the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: «وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون في بضع سنين». That is because the Muslims liked the Romans to prevail over the Persians because they were People of the Book, while the polytheists inclined to the Persians because they were idolaters. When Allah gave the Muslims the good news that the Romans would prevail, the Muslims were glad. Then Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, told the polytheists of Quraysh what had been revealed to them, and Umayya ibn Khalaf said, 'Make a wager with me on that,' and he wagered him five young she-camels for a period of three years. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about the بضع, and he said: 'between three and ten.' He told him of his wager with Ibn Khalaf, and he said to him: 'What made you shorten the period?' He said, 'Trust in Allah and His Messenger.' He said to him: 'Go back to them and raise the stake, and extend the term.' So he added two she-camels and they added two years, and the Romans triumphed over the Persians before the second term ended, confirming Abū Bakr's estimate, may Allah be pleased with him."
(سِمانٍ): the plural of سمينة, and سمين is also pluralised on it; one says رجال سمان as one says نساء سمان. And السمن is the maṣdar of سمن يسمن, so he is سمين. The maṣdar and the noun came in an irregular form, since the regular form of both would be سمنا with fatḥa and فهو سمن, like فرح فرحا فهو فرح. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "سمن يسمن (of the pattern تعب, and in one dialect of the pattern قرب) when his flesh and fat become abundant; it is made transitive by the hamza and by doubling." Among figurative usages: كلام غثّ وسمين ("lean and fat speech"); أسمنت القدر ("I made the pot rich"); دار سمينة ("a fat house") for one with many people; سمّنوا لفلان means "they gave him much"; and سمّنت في الحمد means "I gave much in praise". Ibn Muqbil said:
تركت الخنا لست من أهله ... وسمّنت في الحمد حتى سمن
(I left obscenity, I am not of its people, and I fattened in praise until it grew fat.)
A Bedouin was heard saying to another: "I made the house yours without price so that my standing with you would be fatter." And their land turned to butter and honey (سمنة وعسلة) when both were abundant in it. And in the proverb «سمنكم هريق في أديمكم» ("your butter was spilled in your own skin"), that is, what is spent on you is your own.
(عِجافٌ): the plural of عجفاء in an irregular form; and العجف is emaciation beyond which there is none. The reason عجاف came as a plural of عجفاء, though أفعل and فعلاء are not pluralised on فعال, is that it was carried over onto سمان because it is its opposite; it is their habit to carry a like onto a like and an opposite onto an opposite. The regular form is عجف, like حمراء and حمر.
(رُءْيايَ): The grammarians distinguished between الرؤيا and الرؤية, saying: الرؤيا is the maṣdar of رأى in the sense of dreaming and الرؤية is the maṣdar of رأى in the sense of eye-sight, and they faulted Abū al-Ṭayyib in his saying:
مضى الليل والفضل الذي لك لم يمض ... ورؤياك أحلى في العيون من الغمض
(The night has passed, and the excellence that is yours has not passed; and seeing you is sweeter to the eyes than sleep.)
Abū al-Baqāʾ said in his commentary on the Dīwān of al-Mutanabbī: "الرؤيا is used for sleep only, and of it is His saying, the Exalted, «لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق» and «لا تقصص رؤياك على إخوتك» and «إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون» and «قد صدقت الرؤيا»; all this is about sleep. Had he said «لقياك» it would have been better, but he took الرؤيا to mean الرؤية, like His saying, the Exalted, «وما جعلنا الرؤيا التي أريناك», for by it He did not mean a dream in sleep but waking vision, and that was at night, on the Night of the Journey."
Abū al-Fatḥ ibn Jinnī said: "الرؤيا is in sleep; as for with the eye, I do not know it, and if it comes it is anomalous."
Ibn Hishām said in Awḍaḥ al-Masālik: "الرؤيا is not restricted to the maṣdar of the dream sense, but may occur as the maṣdar of the visual sense, contrary to al-Ḥarīrī and Ibn Mālik, by the evidence of «وما جعلنا الرؤيا التي أريناك إلا فتنة للناس». Ibn ʿAbbās said: it was a vision of the eye. But the well-known usage is for the dream sense."
The author of al-Qāmūs restricted it to the dream: "الرؤيا is what you saw in your sleep", and its plural is رؤى like هدى.
(تَعْبُرُونَ): of the pattern نصر ينصر, and it is also used with doubling like علّم تعليما. In reality عبرت الرؤيا means "I mentioned its outcome and the end of its matter", as you say عبرت النهر when you crossed it until you reached the far side of its width, which is its ʿibr; or it is similar to "I interpreted the dream" when you mention its end, which is its return. The lightened عبرت الرؤيا is what the authorities relied on, and I have seen them deny the doubled عبرت and التعبير and المعبر, though I have come across a verse that al-Mubarrad cited in al-Kāmil by one of the Bedouins:
رأيت رؤيا ثم عبرتها ... وكنت للأحلام عبارا
(I saw a dream, then I interpreted it, and I was an interpreter of dreams.)
In al-Qāmūs: العبار is an intensive of العابر, the interpreter of dreams; and جمل عبار is a camel strong in travel. Today العبر is common with fatḥa and with kasra, and it is the bank and side of a valley; as for العبر with damma, it is the abundant of everything. And العبارة with kasra is a maṣdar, and the noun from عبّر, and the words indicating a meaning; one says "so-and-so has fine expression (ʿibāra)", i.e. clarity, and "this is an expression (ʿibāra) for such-and-such", i.e. it has its meaning and equals it in indication.
(أَضْغاثُ أَحْلامٍ): their confusions and falsehoods, and whatever there is of them from the self's talk or the devil's whispering. The origin of الأضغاث is what is gathered of mixed plants and bundled, the singular being ضغث, and it was borrowed for that. The annexation is in the sense of min, i.e. أضغاث من أحلام. In the proverb: «ضغث على إبالة»; الإبّالة, with kasra of the hamza and doubled bāʾ, is a bundle of grass and firewood, and الضغث is a handful of grass mixing fresh and dry. The meaning of the proverb is "a calamity upon another"; it is also used as a proverb for a man who loads his companion with something disagreeable and then wants it from him.
(ادَّكَرَ): with dāl, which is the eloquent form, and واذّكر with dhāl is permitted. Its origin is اذتكر, of the pattern افتعل from الذكر; the tāʾ of the pattern fell after the dhāl and was changed to dāl; then two close letters met, so the first was changed to the kind of the second and assimilated.
(أُمَّةٍ): with damma on the hamza, doubled mīm and a nunated tāʾ; it is the long period. الأمة is well-known, and الإمة with kasra of the hamza is "favour", and it was also read so. ʿAdī said:
ثم بعد الفلاح والملك والإمة ووارتهم هناك القبور
(Then after prosperity, kingship and favour, the graves covered them there.)

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ ناجٍ مِنْهُمَا اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ): وقال is conjoined to what precedes, and its agent is Yūsuf; وللذي is attached to it, and the clause ظن is a ṣila, the agent of ظن also being Yūsuf; أن with what lies in its sphere stands in the place of the two objects of ظن; inna and its noun, and ناج its khabar; ومنهما is a ḥāl, i.e. "the saved one being one of the two", namely the cupbearer; the clause اذكرني is the content of the saying; وعند ربك is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فَأَنْساهُ الشَّيْطانُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ فَلَبِثَ فِي السِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ): فأنساه الشيطان: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أنساه is a verb and an object, and the pronoun refers back to the cupbearer, and الشيطان is the agent. The meaning: "the devil made him forget to mention Yūsuf to the king." It is also said: "Yūsuf was made to forget the mention of his Lord when he entrusted his affair to another." Many commentators held that the one whom the devil made forget the mention of his Lord was the one who was saved of the two servants, namely the cupbearer. This was preferred on the ground that the devil has no way against the prophets. It was answered that the forgetfulness occurred from Yūsuf and was attributed to the devil figuratively, and that prophets are not immune from forgetting except in what they convey from Allah, Glory be to Him. It is authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said:
«I am only a human being like you; I forget as you forget; so when I forget, remind me.» It was also preferred on the ground that forgetfulness is not a sin, so if the one whom the devil made forget the mention of his Lord were Yūsuf, he would not deserve punishment for that by staying in prison for several years. It was answered that forgetting here is leaving, and that he was punished for seeking help from other than Allah, Glory be to Him. What supports the return of the pronoun to Yūsuf is what follows it: «فلبث في السجن بضع سنين»; and what supports its return to the one saved of the two servants is His saying later on: «وقال الذي نجا منهما وادكر بعد أمة». ذكر is a second object. فلبث: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لبث is a verb with a latent agent; وفي السجن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and بضع سنين is accusative as an adverbial, attached to لبث.
(وَقالَ الْمَلِكُ إِنِّي أَرى سَبْعَ بَقَراتٍ سِمانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجافٌ): inna and its noun, and the clause أرى is its khabar; سبع بقرات is a direct object, and سمان an adjective of بقرات. Why the cows were described and not "seven" will come in the section on Benefits. ويأكلهن سبع: an imperfect verb, an object and an agent, and عجاف an adjective of سبع; the clause يأكلهن is in the position of the accusative as a second object of أرى. He used the imperfect to bring the scene to mind. (وَسَبْعَ سُنْبُلاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يابِساتٍ): وسبع is conjoined to the first سبع, and سنبلات is muḍāf ilayhi, خضر an adjective of سنبلات, and أخر is conjoined to سبع (the discussion of its being a diptote will come in the section on Benefits), and يابسات is an adjective of أخر. (يا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي فِي رُءْيايَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّءْيا تَعْبُرُونَ): أفتوني is an imperative indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being the agent and the yāʾ the object; وفي رؤياي is attached to أفتوني; إن is conditional, and كنتم is kāna with its noun, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the clause تعبرون is the khabar of كنتم, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "then give me a ruling on my dream". As for his saying للرؤيا, the preposition and its genitive noun have several possibilities. One: the lām is for clarification, as in His saying «وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين»; it and its genitive noun are in the position of an accusative ḥāl. Or the lām is for strengthening, because when the governed element precedes the governor it is not as strong in operating on it as it is when it follows it, so it is reinforced with it, just as the active participle is reinforced with it when you say عابر للرؤيا, due to its lowness from the verb in strength; so it is in the rule of the redundant and attaches to nothing; it was added merely for strengthening. And it is permissible that it be the khabar of كنتم, as you say كان فلان لهذا الأمر when he is capable of it and in command of it; in that case the clause تعبرون is a second khabar of كنتم. Al-Mubarrad said in al-Kāmil: This lām is added to the object in the sense of its being added in annexation; you say هذا ضارب زيدا and هذا ضارب لزيد, because it does not change the meaning of the annexation when you say هذا ضارب زيد and ضارب له; and in the Qur'an «وأمرت لأن أكون أول المسلمين» and likewise «إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون». (قالُوا أَضْغاثُ أَحْلامٍ وَما نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ الْأَحْلامِ بِعالِمِينَ): قالوا is a verb and an agent; أضغاث أحلام is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "these are confusions of dreams and mixtures of fancies", and the clause is the content of the saying; the secret of their pluralising it will come in the section on Rhetoric. وما: the wāw is a conjunction and ما is the Ḥijāzī negative; نحن is its noun; وبتأويل is attached to عالمين; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition and عالمين is genitive by the bāʾ in form, accusative in position as the khabar of ليس. (وَقالَ الَّذِي نَجا مِنْهُما وَادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ): The wāw is a conjunction, and قال الذي is a verb and an agent, the clause نجا is a ṣila, ومنهما is a ḥāl, and وادكر is conjoined to نجا; وبعد أمة is attached to ادكر. It is permissible that the wāw be circumstantial, and the clause نجا a ḥāl from the relative or from its returning pronoun, i.e. the agent of نجا. (أَنَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِتَأْوِيلِهِ فَأَرْسِلُونِ): أنا is a mubtadaʾ and the clause أنبئكم its khabar, the kāf being its object; وبتأويله is attached to أنبئكم; فأرسلون: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and أرسلوني is an imperative, an agent and an object, i.e. "if you wish the interpretation of the dream, then send me". (يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا الصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنا فِي سَبْعِ بَقَراتٍ سِمانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنْبُلاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يابِساتٍ): An omitted element is necessary, i.e. "so they sent him, and Yūsuf came in the prison and said". Yūsuf is the one addressed from which the vocative particle is omitted; أيها is accusative in position on the way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), because it is indeclinable on damma, and الصديق is a badal of it or an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān), following it by wording; the discussion of ikhtiṣāṣ will come in the section on Benefits. أفتنا is an imperative indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, its agent latent, "you", and نا an object; وفي سبع is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أفتنا; بقرات is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause يأكلهن سبع عجاف is an adjective of بقرات, and what follows is conjoined to it. (لَعَلِّي أَرْجِعُ إِلَى النَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ): laʿalla and its noun, and the clause أرجع is its khabar; وإلى الناس is attached to أرجع; and لعلهم يعلمون is like it. (قالَ: تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَباً): The clause تزرعون is the content of the saying, and سبع سنين is an adverbial attached to تزرعون; and دأبا is a ḥāl from those addressed, i.e. "diligently", or a maṣdar of an omitted verb, i.e. تدأبون دأبا ("you labour in labour").
(فَما حَصَدْتُمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِي سُنْبُلِهِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ): The fāʾ is a conjunction, and ما may be conditional or relative, and it is in the position of an accusative fronted object of حصدتم in both cases; حصدتم is a verb and an agent; فذروه: the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, or of the relative because of the scent of condition in it; and ذروه is a verb, an agent and an object; وفي سنبله is attached to فذروه; إلا is a particle of exception, and قليلا is an excepted noun that must be accusative; ومما is an adjective of قليلا and the clause تأكلون is a ṣila. (ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ سَبْعٌ شِدادٌ): ثم is a particle of conjunction and delay, and يأتي is an imperfect verb; ومن بعد ذلك is a ḥāl; سبع is the agent of يأتي and شداد an adjective of سبع. (يَأْكُلْنَ ما قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ): The clause يأكلن is a second adjective of سبع, the nūn being the agent and ما an object; the clause قدمتم is the ṣila of ما, and لهن is attached to قدمتم; إلا is a particle of exception, قليلا is excepted, ومما is an adjective of قليلا, and the clause تحصنون is a ṣila. (ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ عامٌ فِيهِ يُغاثُ النَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ)
Likewise a conjunction, and the clause فيه يغاث الناس is an adjective of عام; ويعصرون is conjoined to يغاث, i.e. "they press the grapes and the like".

* Rhetoric:
1- Exaggeration:
They pluralised the word الضغث, saying أضغاث أحلام, and made it the khabar of a single dream, to exaggerate in describing the dream as false, or because it comprised mutually different things. The plural wording, as it indicates a multitude of entities, also indicates exaggeration in the attribution, as in their saying "so-and-so rides horses and wears turbans" of one who owns only one mare and a single turban.

2- Negating a thing by affirming it:
This was pointed to earlier and we add some expansion here, for it is among the beauties of speech: if you consider it, you find its inner meaning is negation and its outer is affirmation. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
على لا حب لا يهتدى بمناره ... إذا سافه العود النباطي جرجرا
(On a road with no clear track, which is not guided by its landmark; when the old Nabaṭī camel sniffs it, it groans.)
By his saying لا يهتدى بمناره he did not mean that it has a landmark which does not guide, but meant that it has no landmark at all, let alone being guided by it. Likewise the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā:
بأرض خلاء لا يسدّ وصيدها ... علي ومعروفي بها غير منكر
(In an empty land whose threshold is not closed against me, and my kindness in it is not disowned.)
He affirmed for it in wording a threshold, but meant only that it has no threshold that could be closed against him. Connected with this is the saying of al-Zubayr ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, mentioning ʿUmayla ibn al-Sabbāq ibn ʿAbd al-Dār, who was his drinking companion and friend:
صبحت بهم طلقا يراح إلى الندى ... إذا ما انتشى لم تحتضره صاقره
ضعيفا يحث الكأس قبض بنانه ... كليلا على وجه النديم أظافره
(I greeted them at morning with one cheerful, going out to generosity, who, when he is merry, is not attended by his hawk-claws; weak, his fingertips' grip urges the cup on, his nails blunt upon the face of his boon-companion.)
[Translator's note: the Arabic of these two verses, and the explanation below, is as in the source; the wording «صاقره» in the first verse differs from «مفاقره» in the explanation.]
The outer meaning of his words is that he scratches the face of his boon-companion, except that his nails are blunt; but in reality he meant that he does not claw the face of his companion and does nothing of that sort. Likewise his saying لم تحتضره مفاقره, i.e. he has no needs (mafāqir) that would attend him. What is more eloquent than that will come in its place, namely His saying, the Exalted: «لا يسألون الناس إلحافا», that is, they do not ask at all. And in the verse we are concerned with, the Creator, the Exalted, meant to negate false dreams in particular, as if they said: "And there is no interpretation of false dreams for us to be knowers of it." And the beauty is completed by correspondence: the king had said to them first «إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون», to show that in his knowledge they were not knowers of it, since he used the word «إن», which conveys doubt, hoping for their admission of shortcoming, matching the king's doubt which he put in the form of a question about whether they were knowers of dreams at all. And the saying of the youth «أنا أنبئكم بتأويله» up to «لعلي أرجع إلى الناس لعلهم يعلمون» is also evidence of that. Glory be to the Speaker of these words.

* Benefits:
1- He, Glory be to Him, put His saying «سمان» as an adjective of the specified noun (al-mumayyaz), which is بقرات, and not of the specifier (al-mumayyiz), which is سبع. The difference between the two matters, both permissible in the rules of grammar, is that if you make it an adjective of بقرات, you mean to specify the seven by a kind of cows, namely the fat ones among them specifically, not by their genus; and if you make it an adjective of سبع, you mean to specify the seven by the genus of cows, not by a particular kind of them, and then you go back and describe the specified, which is by genus, with fatness.
2- The word أخر indicates that the dry ears were seven like the green, without stating the number. That is because the speech is built on its flowing toward this number in the fat cows, the lean cows and the green ears, so the meaning of أخر must include the seven, and His saying وأخر يابسات means وسبعا أخر ("and seven others").
3- أخر:
An adjective turned (maʿdūl) from the pattern آخر. The turning of an adjective has two places:
A- Numbers on the pattern «فعال ومفعل», like أحاد and موحد, ثناء and مثنى, ثلاث and مثلث, رباع and مربع; they are turned from واحد واحد and اثنين اثنين, etc. If you say جاء القوم مثنى the meaning is that they came two by two. They said that turning in numbers is heard from the Arabs up to four, but the grammarians extended that by analogy to ten; and the truth is that it is heard for one and ten and what lies between. Abū al-Ṭayyib said:
أحاد أم سداس في أحاد ... لييلتنا المنوطة بالتناد
(Is it one by one or six within ones, our little night that is tied to the Day of Calling?)
B- أخر in your saying مررت بنساء أخر, and the Exalted said «فعدة من أيام أخر»; it is the plural of أخرى, the feminine of آخر, and آخر, with fatḥa on the khāʾ, is an elative on the pattern أفعل in the sense of "other"; the analogy would have been to say مررت بنساء آخر, as one says مررت بنساء أفضل, because an elative stripped of من, of al and of annexation is neither feminised, dualised nor pluralised.
4- Specification (al-ikhtiṣāṣ):
It is putting a noun in the accusative by an obligatorily omitted verb, its implied form being أخص or أعني, and this noun occurs only after a pronoun to clarify what is meant by it, as in: نحن العرب نكرم الضيف ("we Arabs honour the guest"); نحن is a mubtadaʾ and the clause نكرم الضيف is the khabar, and العرب is accusative by specification through an omitted verb, its implied form being أخص, and the clause of the omitted verb is parenthetical between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar. The intention is not to predicate "the Arabs" of نحن; rather, it is that honouring the guest is particular to the Arabs and restricted to them. Of it is the saying of Abū ʿUbāda al-Buḥturī:
نحن أبناء يعرب، أعرب النا ... س لسانا وأنضر الناس عودا
(We are the sons of Yaʿrub, the most eloquent of people in tongue and the most flourishing of people in stock.)
Specification may also be with the word أيها and أيتها, which are used as they are used in the vocative, so they are indeclinable on damma and are in the position of the accusative through an obligatorily omitted أخص, and what follows them is a noun with al that must be nominative as an adjective or a badal of their wording; it is not permitted to put it in the accusative as following their position, as in the noble verse.
